+\begin{lemma}[Stable critical translation remainder]
+\label{lem:stable-critical-translation-remainder}
+Let \(d\ge1\), \(0<\alpha<2\), \(p=p_{\alpha,d}\),
+\(q=q_{\alpha,d}\), and \(m=\lfloor p\rfloor\).  If
+\(T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)\) is the Taylor polynomial of
+\(F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\) at \(z=0\) through degree \(m\), then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth}
+ c_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+ \le \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}^q
+ \le C_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}.
+\end{equation}
+Moreover,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}
+ \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}
+ \begin{cases}
+  |z|^{m+1},&|z|\le1,\\
+  |z|^p,&|z|>1,
+ \end{cases}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}|z|^p.
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The standard stable-kernel estimates recorded as properties (G)(ii)--(iii)
+by Ishige--Kawakami--Michihisa
+\cite{IshigeKawakamiMichihisa2017} give, with constants depending on the
+chosen stable scale,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}
+ c(1+|y|)^{-\beta}\le p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)
+ \le C(1+|y|)^{-\beta},\qquad
+ |\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)|
+ \le C_\eta(1+|y|)^{-\beta-|\eta|}.
+\end{equation}
+In particular every quotient
+\(\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}/p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) is bounded.  The upper
+bound in \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} follows from
+\[
+ \begin{aligned}
+ \int p_1(y-z)^q p_1(y)^{1-q}\dd y
+ &\le C\int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta q}
+              (1+|y|)^{\beta(q-1)}\dd y\\
+ &\le C(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+       \int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta}\dd y,
+ \end{aligned}
+\]
+where \(p_1=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) and
+\(1+|y|\le(1+|z|)(1+|y-z|)\).  The final integral is finite because
+\(\beta>d\).  For the lower bound, integrate over \(|y-z|\le1\) and use
+\eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}; this gives the claimed power
+for \(|z|\ge2\).  Positivity and continuity on bounded \(z\)-sets complete
+the estimate.
+
+For \(|z|\le1\), Taylor's formula and the bounded derivative quotients give
+the pointwise bound
+\(|F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)|\le C|z|^{m+1}\), uniformly
+in \(y\).  For \(|z|>1\), \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} gives
+\(\|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_q\le C|z|^{\beta(1-1/q)}\).  The Taylor
+coefficients are bounded, so
+\(\|T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_q\le C|z|^m\).  Finally,
+\[
+ \beta(1-1/q)\le p,\qquad m\le p<m+1,
+\]
+with equality in the first relation when \(\beta>4\).  These observations
+prove \eqref{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}.
+\end{proof}

-\(t_j=\kappa R_jw_j^{1/(d+1)}\), the same binary data-processing estimate
-gives
+We first prove the obstruction below two moments.  If
+\(\limsup_{s\to\infty}s^4H_{\alpha,d}(s)<\infty\), Pinsker's inequality
+and scaling give, for every fixed \(\xi\in\RR^d\),
+\[
+ |\widehat p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(\xi)|
+ |\varphi_X(\xi/s)-1|
+ \le \|p_1^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu_s-p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\|_1
+ \le \sqrt{2H_{\alpha,d}(s)}=O(s^{-2}),
+\]
+where \(\nu_s\) is the law of \(X/s\).  Since the stable characteristic
+function never vanishes, take \(\xi=e\) for a unit vector \(e\), multiply
+the real part by \(s^2\), and use Fatou's lemma to obtain
+\[
+ \frac12\EE(e\cdot X)^2
+ \le \liminf_{s\to\infty}s^2
+       \EE[1-\cos((e\cdot X)/s)]<\infty.
+\]
+Thus bounded scaled entropy forces finite covariance.  Given \(0<r<2\),
+choose \(a\in(\max\{1,r\},2)\) and put symmetric masses proportional to
+\(n^{-a-1}\) at \(\pm ne_1\), with the remaining mass at zero.  This law
+has mean zero and finite \(r\)th moment but infinite variance, so its scaled
+entropy has infinite limsup.
+
+It remains to prove optimality between two and \(p\) when \(\beta>4\).
+Fix \(2\le r<p\), choose positive \(a_j\) with \(\sum_ja_j<\infty\), and
+put symmetric masses \(w_j/2\) at \(\pm R_je_1\), where
+\(w_j=a_jR_j^{-r}\).  Add a sufficiently small bounded symmetric spanning
+component.  The resulting law has positive-definite finite covariance and
+finite \(r\)th moment.  Set
+\[
+ s_j=\kappa R_jw_j^{1/\beta},\qquad
+ A_j=B(R_je_1,s_j).
+\]
+The component at \(R_je_1\) gives
+\((p_{s_j}^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu)(A_j)\ge c_{\alpha,d}w_j\).  On the other hand,
+\eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds} and \(s_j/R_j\to0\) give
+\[
+ p_{s_j}^{(\alpha,d)}(A_j)
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}(s_j/R_j)^\beta
+ =C_{\alpha,d}\kappa^\beta w_j.
+\]
+Choose \(\kappa\) so that the second Bernoulli mass is a fixed small
+fraction of the first.  Data processing to
+\(\{A_j,A_j^c\}\) then yields \(H_{\alpha,d}(s_j)\ge c w_j\), and hence
 \[
- t_j^4H_d(t_j)\ge c_dR_j^4w_j^{1+4/(d+1)}
- =c_d\alpha_j^{q_d}R_j^{4-rq_d}.
+ s_j^4H_{\alpha,d}(s_j)
+ \ge cR_j^4w_j^{1+4/\beta}
+ =ca_j^{q_{\alpha,d}}R_j^{4-rq_{\alpha,d}}.
 \]
-Since \(r<p_d=4/q_d\), the exponent of \(R_j\) is positive.  Recursive
-choice of the radii makes this expression unbounded while preserving the
-finite \(r\)th moment and, after adding a bounded spanning component, a
-positive-definite covariance.
+Here \(q_{\alpha,d}=1+4/\beta\) and
+\(r<p=4/q_{\alpha,d}\), so the exponent of \(R_j\) is positive.
+Recursive choice of the radii makes \(s_j\to\infty\) and the last display
+unbounded while preserving all moment assertions.
 \end{proof}

+centred isotropic strictly \(\alpha\)-stable law on \(\RR^d\), and use the
+spatial-scale normalization
+\[

+strictly stable kernel.  Put

+ \beta=d+\alpha,\qquad
+ q_{\alpha,d}:=\min\left\{2,1+\frac4\beta\right\},\qquad

+ =\max\left\{2,\frac{4(d+\alpha)}{d+\alpha+4}\right\}.
+\end{equation}
+Write \(\Omega_{\alpha,d}(\dd y)=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)\dd y\) and
+\[
+ F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)
+ :=\frac{p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y-z)}{p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)}.

+\begin{lemma}[Stable critical translation remainder]
+\label{lem:stable-critical-translation-remainder}
+Let \(d\ge1\), \(0<\alpha<2\), \(p=p_{\alpha,d}\),
+\(q=q_{\alpha,d}\), and \(m=\lfloor p\rfloor\).  If
+\(T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)\) is the Taylor polynomial of
+\(F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\) at \(z=0\) through degree \(m\), then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth}
+ c_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+ \le \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}^q
+ \le C_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}.
+\end{equation}
+Moreover,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}
+ \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}
+ \begin{cases}
+  |z|^{m+1},&|z|\le1,\\
+  |z|^p,&|z|>1,
+ \end{cases}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}|z|^p.
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The standard stable-kernel estimates recorded as properties (G)(ii)--(iii)
+by Ishige--Kawakami--Michihisa
+\cite{IshigeKawakamiMichihisa2017} give, with constants depending on the
+chosen stable scale,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}
+ c(1+|y|)^{-\beta}\le p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)
+ \le C(1+|y|)^{-\beta},\qquad
+ |\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)|
+ \le C_\eta(1+|y|)^{-\beta-|\eta|}.
+\end{equation}
+In particular every quotient
+\(\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}/p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) is bounded.  The upper
+bound in \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} follows from
+\[
+ \begin{aligned}
+ \int p_1(y-z)^q p_1(y)^{1-q}\dd y
+ &\le C\int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta q}
+              (1+|y|)^{\beta(q-1)}\dd y\\
+ &\le C(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+       \int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta}\dd y,
+ \end{aligned}
+\]
+where \(p_1=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) and
+\(1+|y|\le(1+|z|)(1+|y-z|)\).  The final integral is finite because
+\(\beta>d\).  For the lower bound, integrate over \(|y-z|\le1\) and use
+\eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}; this gives the claimed power
+for \(|z|\ge2\).  Positivity and continuity on bounded \(z\)-sets complete
+the estimate.
+
+For \(|z|\le1\), Taylor's formula and the bounded derivative quotients give
+the pointwise bound
+\(|F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)|\le C|z|^{m+1}\), uniformly
+in \(y\).  For \(|z|>1\), \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} gives
+\(\|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_q\le C|z|^{\beta(1-1/q)}\).  The Taylor
+coefficients are bounded, so
+\(\|T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_q\le C|z|^m\).  Finally,
+\[
+ \beta(1-1/q)\le p,\qquad m\le p<m+1,
+\]
+with equality in the first relation when \(\beta>4\).  These observations
+prove \eqref{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}.
+\end{proof}

+Write \(\Omega_{\alpha,d}(\dd y)=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)\dd y\) and

+\begin{lemma}[Stable critical translation remainder]
+\label{lem:stable-critical-translation-remainder}
+Let \(d\ge1\), \(0<\alpha<2\), \(p=p_{\alpha,d}\),
+\(q=q_{\alpha,d}\), and \(m=\lfloor p\rfloor\).  If
+\(T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)\) is the Taylor polynomial of
+\(F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\) at \(z=0\) through degree \(m\), then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth}
+ c_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+ \le \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}^q
+ \le C_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}.
+\end{equation}
+Moreover,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}
+ \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}
+ \begin{cases}
+  |z|^{m+1},&|z|\le1,\\
+  |z|^p,&|z|>1,
+ \end{cases}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}|z|^p.
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The standard stable-kernel estimates recorded as properties (G)(ii)--(iii)
+by Ishige--Kawakami--Michihisa
+\cite{IshigeKawakamiMichihisa2017} give, with constants depending on the
+chosen stable scale,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}
+ c(1+|y|)^{-\beta}\le p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)
+ \le C(1+|y|)^{-\beta},\qquad
+ |\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)|
+ \le C_\eta(1+|y|)^{-\beta-|\eta|}.
+\end{equation}
+In particular every quotient
+\(\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}/p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) is bounded.  The upper
+bound in \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} follows from
+\[
+ \begin{aligned}
+ \int p_1(y-z)^q p_1(y)^{1-q}\dd y
+ &\le C\int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta q}
+              (1+|y|)^{\beta(q-1)}\dd y\\
+ &\le C(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+       \int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta}\dd y,
+ \end{aligned}
+\]
+where \(p_1=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) and
+\(1+|y|\le(1+|z|)(1+|y-z|)\).  The final integral is finite because
+\(\beta>d\).  For the lower bound, integrate over \(|y-z|\le1\) and use
+\eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}; this gives the claimed power
+for \(|z|\ge2\).  Positivity and continuity on bounded \(z\)-sets complete
+the estimate.
+
+For \(|z|\le1\), Taylor's formula and the bounded derivative quotients give
+the pointwise bound
+\(|F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)|\le C|z|^{m+1}\), uniformly
+in \(y\).  For \(|z|>1\), \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} gives
+\(\|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_q\le C|z|^{\beta(1-1/q)}\).  The Taylor
+coefficients are bounded, so
+\(\|T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_q\le C|z|^m\).  Finally,
+\[
+ \beta(1-1/q)\le p,\qquad m\le p<m+1,
+\]
+with equality in the first relation when \(\beta>4\).  These observations
+prove \eqref{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}.
+\end{proof}

+\begin{lemma}[Stable critical translation remainder]
+\label{lem:stable-critical-translation-remainder}
+Let \(d\ge1\), \(0<\alpha<2\), \(p=p_{\alpha,d}\),
+\(q=q_{\alpha,d}\), and \(m=\lfloor p\rfloor\).  If
+\(T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)\) is the Taylor polynomial of
+\(F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\) at \(z=0\) through degree \(m\), then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth}
+ c_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+ \le \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}^q
+ \le C_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}.
+\end{equation}
+Moreover,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}
+ \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}
+ \begin{cases}
+  |z|^{m+1},&|z|\le1,\\
+  |z|^p,&|z|>1,
+ \end{cases}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}|z|^p.
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The standard stable-kernel estimates recorded as properties (G)(ii)--(iii)
+by Ishige--Kawakami--Michihisa
+\cite{IshigeKawakamiMichihisa2017} give, with constants depending on the
+chosen stable scale,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}
+ c(1+|y|)^{-\beta}\le p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)
+ \le C(1+|y|)^{-\beta},\qquad
+ |\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)|
+ \le C_\eta(1+|y|)^{-\beta-|\eta|}.
+\end{equation}
+In particular every quotient
+\(\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}/p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) is bounded.  The upper
+bound in \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} follows from
+\[
+ \begin{aligned}
+ \int p_1(y-z)^q p_1(y)^{1-q}\dd y
+ &\le C\int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta q}
+              (1+|y|)^{\beta(q-1)}\dd y\\
+ &\le C(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+       \int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta}\dd y,
+ \end{aligned}
+\]
+where \(p_1=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) and
+\(1+|y|\le(1+|z|)(1+|y-z|)\).  The final integral is finite because
+\(\beta>d\).  For the lower bound, integrate over \(|y-z|\le1\) and use
+\eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}; this gives the claimed power
+for \(|z|\ge2\).  Positivity and continuity on bounded \(z\)-sets complete
+the estimate.
+
+For \(|z|\le1\), Taylor's formula and the bounded derivative quotients give
+the pointwise bound
+\(|F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)|\le C|z|^{m+1}\), uniformly
+in \(y\).  For \(|z|>1\), \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} gives
+\(\|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_q\le C|z|^{\beta(1-1/q)}\).  The Taylor
+coefficients are bounded, so
+\(\|T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_q\le C|z|^m\).  Finally,
+\[
+ \beta(1-1/q)\le p,\qquad m\le p<m+1,
+\]
+with equality in the first relation when \(\beta>4\).  These observations
+prove \eqref{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}.
+\end{proof}

+\begin{lemma}[Stable critical translation remainder]
+\label{lem:stable-critical-translation-remainder}
+Let \(d\ge1\), \(0<\alpha<2\), \(p=p_{\alpha,d}\),
+\(q=q_{\alpha,d}\), and \(m=\lfloor p\rfloor\).  If
+\(T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)\) is the Taylor polynomial of
+\(F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\) at \(z=0\) through degree \(m\), then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth}
+ c_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+ \le \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}^q
+ \le C_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}.
+\end{equation}
+Moreover,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}
+ \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}
+ \begin{cases}
+  |z|^{m+1},&|z|\le1,\\
+  |z|^p,&|z|>1,
+ \end{cases}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}|z|^p.
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The standard stable-kernel estimates recorded as properties (G)(ii)--(iii)
+by Ishige--Kawakami--Michihisa
+\cite{IshigeKawakamiMichihisa2017} give, with constants depending on the
+chosen stable scale,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}
+ c(1+|y|)^{-\beta}\le p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)
+ \le C(1+|y|)^{-\beta},\qquad
+ |\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)|
+ \le C_\eta(1+|y|)^{-\beta-|\eta|}.
+\end{equation}
+In particular every quotient
+\(\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}/p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) is bounded.  The upper
+bound in \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} follows from
+\[
+ \begin{aligned}
+ \int p_1(y-z)^q p_1(y)^{1-q}\dd y
+ &\le C\int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta q}
+              (1+|y|)^{\beta(q-1)}\dd y\\
+ &\le C(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+       \int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta}\dd y,
+ \end{aligned}
+\]
+where \(p_1=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) and
+\(1+|y|\le(1+|z|)(1+|y-z|)\).  The final integral is finite because
+\(\beta>d\).  For the lower bound, integrate over \(|y-z|\le1\) and use
+\eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}; this gives the claimed power
+for \(|z|\ge2\).  Positivity and continuity on bounded \(z\)-sets complete
+the estimate.
+
+For \(|z|\le1\), Taylor's formula and the bounded derivative quotients give
+the pointwise bound
+\(|F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)|\le C|z|^{m+1}\), uniformly
+in \(y\).  For \(|z|>1\), \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} gives
+\(\|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_q\le C|z|^{\beta(1-1/q)}\).  The Taylor
+coefficients are bounded, so
+\(\|T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_q\le C|z|^m\).  Finally,
+\[
+ \beta(1-1/q)\le p,\qquad m\le p<m+1,
+\]
+with equality in the first relation when \(\beta>4\).  These observations
+prove \eqref{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}.
+\end{proof}

+\begin{lemma}[Stable critical translation remainder]
+\label{lem:stable-critical-translation-remainder}
+Let \(d\ge1\), \(0<\alpha<2\), \(p=p_{\alpha,d}\),
+\(q=q_{\alpha,d}\), and \(m=\lfloor p\rfloor\).  If
+\(T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)\) is the Taylor polynomial of
+\(F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\) at \(z=0\) through degree \(m\), then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth}
+ c_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+ \le \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}^q
+ \le C_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}.
+\end{equation}
+Moreover,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}
+ \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}
+ \begin{cases}
+  |z|^{m+1},&|z|\le1,\\
+  |z|^p,&|z|>1,
+ \end{cases}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}|z|^p.
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The standard stable-kernel estimates recorded as properties (G)(ii)--(iii)
+by Ishige--Kawakami--Michihisa
+\cite{IshigeKawakamiMichihisa2017} give, with constants depending on the
+chosen stable scale,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}
+ c(1+|y|)^{-\beta}\le p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)
+ \le C(1+|y|)^{-\beta},\qquad
+ |\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)|
+ \le C_\eta(1+|y|)^{-\beta-|\eta|}.
+\end{equation}
+In particular every quotient
+\(\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}/p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) is bounded.  The upper
+bound in \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} follows from
+\[
+ \begin{aligned}
+ \int p_1(y-z)^q p_1(y)^{1-q}\dd y
+ &\le C\int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta q}
+              (1+|y|)^{\beta(q-1)}\dd y\\
+ &\le C(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+       \int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta}\dd y,
+ \end{aligned}
+\]
+where \(p_1=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) and
+\(1+|y|\le(1+|z|)(1+|y-z|)\).  The final integral is finite because
+\(\beta>d\).  For the lower bound, integrate over \(|y-z|\le1\) and use
+\eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}; this gives the claimed power
+for \(|z|\ge2\).  Positivity and continuity on bounded \(z\)-sets complete
+the estimate.
+
+For \(|z|\le1\), Taylor's formula and the bounded derivative quotients give
+the pointwise bound
+\(|F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)|\le C|z|^{m+1}\), uniformly
+in \(y\).  For \(|z|>1\), \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} gives
+\(\|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_q\le C|z|^{\beta(1-1/q)}\).  The Taylor
+coefficients are bounded, so
+\(\|T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_q\le C|z|^m\).  Finally,
+\[
+ \beta(1-1/q)\le p,\qquad m\le p<m+1,
+\]
+with equality in the first relation when \(\beta>4\).  These observations
+prove \eqref{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}.
+\end{proof}

+Write \(\Omega_{\alpha,d}(\dd y)=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)\dd y\) and

+\begin{lemma}[Stable critical translation remainder]
+\label{lem:stable-critical-translation-remainder}
+Let \(d\ge1\), \(0<\alpha<2\), \(p=p_{\alpha,d}\),
+\(q=q_{\alpha,d}\), and \(m=\lfloor p\rfloor\).  If
+\(T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)\) is the Taylor polynomial of
+\(F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\) at \(z=0\) through degree \(m\), then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth}
+ c_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+ \le \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}^q
+ \le C_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}.
+\end{equation}
+Moreover,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}
+ \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}
+ \begin{cases}
+  |z|^{m+1},&|z|\le1,\\
+  |z|^p,&|z|>1,
+ \end{cases}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}|z|^p.
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The standard stable-kernel estimates recorded as properties (G)(ii)--(iii)
+by Ishige--Kawakami--Michihisa
+\cite{IshigeKawakamiMichihisa2017} give, with constants depending on the
+chosen stable scale,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}
+ c(1+|y|)^{-\beta}\le p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)
+ \le C(1+|y|)^{-\beta},\qquad
+ |\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)|
+ \le C_\eta(1+|y|)^{-\beta-|\eta|}.
+\end{equation}
+In particular every quotient
+\(\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}/p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) is bounded.  The upper
+bound in \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} follows from
+\[
+ \begin{aligned}
+ \int p_1(y-z)^q p_1(y)^{1-q}\dd y
+ &\le C\int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta q}
+              (1+|y|)^{\beta(q-1)}\dd y\\
+ &\le C(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+       \int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta}\dd y,
+ \end{aligned}
+\]
+where \(p_1=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) and
+\(1+|y|\le(1+|z|)(1+|y-z|)\).  The final integral is finite because
+\(\beta>d\).  For the lower bound, integrate over \(|y-z|\le1\) and use
+\eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}; this gives the claimed power
+for \(|z|\ge2\).  Positivity and continuity on bounded \(z\)-sets complete
+the estimate.
+
+For \(|z|\le1\), Taylor's formula and the bounded derivative quotients give
+the pointwise bound
+\(|F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)|\le C|z|^{m+1}\), uniformly
+in \(y\).  For \(|z|>1\), \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} gives
+\(\|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_q\le C|z|^{\beta(1-1/q)}\).  The Taylor
+coefficients are bounded, so
+\(\|T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_q\le C|z|^m\).  Finally,
+\[
+ \beta(1-1/q)\le p,\qquad m\le p<m+1,
+\]
+with equality in the first relation when \(\beta>4\).  These observations
+prove \eqref{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}.
+\end{proof}
+

+\begin{lemma}[Stable critical translation remainder]
+\label{lem:stable-critical-translation-remainder}
+Let \(d\ge1\), \(0<\alpha<2\), \(p=p_{\alpha,d}\),
+\(q=q_{\alpha,d}\), and \(m=\lfloor p\rfloor\).  If
+\(T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)\) is the Taylor polynomial of
+\(F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\) at \(z=0\) through degree \(m\), then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth}
+ c_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+ \le \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}^q
+ \le C_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}.
+\end{equation}
+Moreover,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}
+ \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}
+ \begin{cases}
+  |z|^{m+1},&|z|\le1,\\
+  |z|^p,&|z|>1,
+ \end{cases}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}|z|^p.
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The standard stable-kernel estimates recorded as properties (G)(ii)--(iii)
+by Ishige--Kawakami--Michihisa
+\cite{IshigeKawakamiMichihisa2017} give, with constants depending on the
+chosen stable scale,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}
+ c(1+|y|)^{-\beta}\le p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)
+ \le C(1+|y|)^{-\beta},\qquad
+ |\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)|
+ \le C_\eta(1+|y|)^{-\beta-|\eta|}.
+\end{equation}
+In particular every quotient
+\(\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}/p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) is bounded.  The upper
+bound in \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} follows from
+\[
+ \begin{aligned}
+ \int p_1(y-z)^q p_1(y)^{1-q}\dd y
+ &\le C\int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta q}
+              (1+|y|)^{\beta(q-1)}\dd y\\
+ &\le C(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+       \int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta}\dd y,
+ \end{aligned}
+\]
+where \(p_1=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) and
+\(1+|y|\le(1+|z|)(1+|y-z|)\).  The final integral is finite because
+\(\beta>d\).  For the lower bound, integrate over \(|y-z|\le1\) and use
+\eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}; this gives the claimed power
+for \(|z|\ge2\).  Positivity and continuity on bounded \(z\)-sets complete
+the estimate.
+
+For \(|z|\le1\), Taylor's formula and the bounded derivative quotients give
+the pointwise bound
+\(|F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)|\le C|z|^{m+1}\), uniformly
+in \(y\).  For \(|z|>1\), \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} gives
+\(\|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_q\le C|z|^{\beta(1-1/q)}\).  The Taylor
+coefficients are bounded, so
+\(\|T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_q\le C|z|^m\).  Finally,
+\[
+ \beta(1-1/q)\le p,\qquad m\le p<m+1,
+\]
+with equality in the first relation when \(\beta>4\).  These observations
+prove \eqref{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}.
+\end{proof}

+\end{equation}
+Write \(\Omega_{\alpha,d}(\dd y)=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)\dd y\) and

+ F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)

+\begin{lemma}[Stable critical translation remainder]
+\label{lem:stable-critical-translation-remainder}
+Let \(d\ge1\), \(0<\alpha<2\), \(p=p_{\alpha,d}\),
+\(q=q_{\alpha,d}\), and \(m=\lfloor p\rfloor\).  If
+\(T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)\) is the Taylor polynomial of
+\(F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\) at \(z=0\) through degree \(m\), then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth}
+ c_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+ \le \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}^q
+ \le C_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}.
+\end{equation}
+Moreover,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}
+ \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}
+ \begin{cases}
+  |z|^{m+1},&|z|\le1,\\
+  |z|^p,&|z|>1,
+ \end{cases}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}|z|^p.
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The standard stable-kernel estimates recorded as properties (G)(ii)--(iii)
+by Ishige--Kawakami--Michihisa
+\cite{IshigeKawakamiMichihisa2017} give, with constants depending on the
+chosen stable scale,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}
+ c(1+|y|)^{-\beta}\le p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)
+ \le C(1+|y|)^{-\beta},\qquad
+ |\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)|
+ \le C_\eta(1+|y|)^{-\beta-|\eta|}.
+\end{equation}
+In particular every quotient
+\(\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}/p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) is bounded.  The upper
+bound in \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} follows from
+\[
+ \begin{aligned}
+ \int p_1(y-z)^q p_1(y)^{1-q}\dd y
+ &\le C\int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta q}
+              (1+|y|)^{\beta(q-1)}\dd y\\
+ &\le C(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+       \int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta}\dd y,
+ \end{aligned}
+\]
+where \(p_1=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) and
+\(1+|y|\le(1+|z|)(1+|y-z|)\).  The final integral is finite because
+\(\beta>d\).  For the lower bound, integrate over \(|y-z|\le1\) and use
+\eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}; this gives the claimed power
+for \(|z|\ge2\).  Positivity and continuity on bounded \(z\)-sets complete
+the estimate.
+
+For \(|z|\le1\), Taylor's formula and the bounded derivative quotients give
+the pointwise bound
+\(|F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)|\le C|z|^{m+1}\), uniformly
+in \(y\).  For \(|z|>1\), \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} gives
+\(\|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_q\le C|z|^{\beta(1-1/q)}\).  The Taylor
+coefficients are bounded, so
+\(\|T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_q\le C|z|^m\).  Finally,
+\[
+ \beta(1-1/q)\le p,\qquad m\le p<m+1,
+\]
+with equality in the first relation when \(\beta>4\).  These observations
+prove \eqref{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}.
+\end{proof}

+\begin{lemma}[Stable critical translation remainder]
+\label{lem:stable-critical-translation-remainder}
+Let \(d\ge1\), \(0<\alpha<2\), \(p=p_{\alpha,d}\),
+\(q=q_{\alpha,d}\), and \(m=\lfloor p\rfloor\).  If
+\(T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)\) is the Taylor polynomial of
+\(F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\) at \(z=0\) through degree \(m\), then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth}
+ c_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+ \le \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}^q
+ \le C_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}.
+\end{equation}
+Moreover,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}
+ \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}
+ \begin{cases}
+  |z|^{m+1},&|z|\le1,\\
+  |z|^p,&|z|>1,
+ \end{cases}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}|z|^p.
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The standard stable-kernel estimates recorded as properties (G)(ii)--(iii)
+by Ishige--Kawakami--Michihisa
+\cite{IshigeKawakamiMichihisa2017} give, with constants depending on the
+chosen stable scale,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}
+ c(1+|y|)^{-\beta}\le p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)
+ \le C(1+|y|)^{-\beta},\qquad
+ |\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)|
+ \le C_\eta(1+|y|)^{-\beta-|\eta|}.
+\end{equation}
+In particular every quotient
+\(\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}/p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) is bounded.  The upper
+bound in \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} follows from
+\[
+ \begin{aligned}
+ \int p_1(y-z)^q p_1(y)^{1-q}\dd y
+ &\le C\int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta q}
+              (1+|y|)^{\beta(q-1)}\dd y\\
+ &\le C(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+       \int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta}\dd y,
+ \end{aligned}
+\]
+where \(p_1=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) and
+\(1+|y|\le(1+|z|)(1+|y-z|)\).  The final integral is finite because
+\(\beta>d\).  For the lower bound, integrate over \(|y-z|\le1\) and use
+\eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}; this gives the claimed power
+for \(|z|\ge2\).  Positivity and continuity on bounded \(z\)-sets complete
+the estimate.
+
+For \(|z|\le1\), Taylor's formula and the bounded derivative quotients give
+the pointwise bound
+\(|F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)|\le C|z|^{m+1}\), uniformly
+in \(y\).  For \(|z|>1\), \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} gives
+\(\|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_q\le C|z|^{\beta(1-1/q)}\).  The Taylor
+coefficients are bounded, so
+\(\|T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_q\le C|z|^m\).  Finally,
+\[
+ \beta(1-1/q)\le p,\qquad m\le p<m+1,
+\]
+with equality in the first relation when \(\beta>4\).  These observations
+prove \eqref{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}.
+\end{proof}

+\begin{lemma}[Stable critical translation remainder]
+\label{lem:stable-critical-translation-remainder}
+Let \(d\ge1\), \(0<\alpha<2\), \(p=p_{\alpha,d}\),
+\(q=q_{\alpha,d}\), and \(m=\lfloor p\rfloor\).  If
+\(T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)\) is the Taylor polynomial of
+\(F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\) at \(z=0\) through degree \(m\), then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth}
+ c_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+ \le \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}^q
+ \le C_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}.
+\end{equation}
+Moreover,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}
+ \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}
+ \begin{cases}
+  |z|^{m+1},&|z|\le1,\\
+  |z|^p,&|z|>1,
+ \end{cases}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}|z|^p.
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The standard stable-kernel estimates recorded as properties (G)(ii)--(iii)
+by Ishige--Kawakami--Michihisa
+\cite{IshigeKawakamiMichihisa2017} give, with constants depending on the
+chosen stable scale,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}
+ c(1+|y|)^{-\beta}\le p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)
+ \le C(1+|y|)^{-\beta},\qquad
+ |\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)|
+ \le C_\eta(1+|y|)^{-\beta-|\eta|}.
+\end{equation}
+In particular every quotient
+\(\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}/p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) is bounded.  The upper
+bound in \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} follows from
+\[
+ \begin{aligned}
+ \int p_1(y-z)^q p_1(y)^{1-q}\dd y
+ &\le C\int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta q}
+              (1+|y|)^{\beta(q-1)}\dd y\\
+ &\le C(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+       \int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta}\dd y,
+ \end{aligned}
+\]
+where \(p_1=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) and
+\(1+|y|\le(1+|z|)(1+|y-z|)\).  The final integral is finite because
+\(\beta>d\).  For the lower bound, integrate over \(|y-z|\le1\) and use
+\eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}; this gives the claimed power
+for \(|z|\ge2\).  Positivity and continuity on bounded \(z\)-sets complete
+the estimate.
+
+For \(|z|\le1\), Taylor's formula and the bounded derivative quotients give
+the pointwise bound
+\(|F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)|\le C|z|^{m+1}\), uniformly
+in \(y\).  For \(|z|>1\), \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} gives
+\(\|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_q\le C|z|^{\beta(1-1/q)}\).  The Taylor
+coefficients are bounded, so
+\(\|T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_q\le C|z|^m\).  Finally,
+\[
+ \beta(1-1/q)\le p,\qquad m\le p<m+1,
+\]
+with equality in the first relation when \(\beta>4\).  These observations
+prove \eqref{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}.
+\end{proof}

+\begin{lemma}[Stable critical translation remainder]
+\label{lem:stable-critical-translation-remainder}
+Let \(d\ge1\), \(0<\alpha<2\), \(p=p_{\alpha,d}\),
+\(q=q_{\alpha,d}\), and \(m=\lfloor p\rfloor\).  If
+\(T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)\) is the Taylor polynomial of
+\(F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\) at \(z=0\) through degree \(m\), then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth}
+ c_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+ \le \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}^q
+ \le C_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}.
+\end{equation}
+Moreover,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}
+ \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}
+ \begin{cases}
+  |z|^{m+1},&|z|\le1,\\
+  |z|^p,&|z|>1,
+ \end{cases}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}|z|^p.
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The standard stable-kernel estimates recorded as properties (G)(ii)--(iii)
+by Ishige--Kawakami--Michihisa
+\cite{IshigeKawakamiMichihisa2017} give, with constants depending on the
+chosen stable scale,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}
+ c(1+|y|)^{-\beta}\le p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)
+ \le C(1+|y|)^{-\beta},\qquad
+ |\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)|
+ \le C_\eta(1+|y|)^{-\beta-|\eta|}.
+\end{equation}
+In particular every quotient
+\(\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}/p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) is bounded.  The upper
+bound in \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} follows from
+\[
+ \begin{aligned}
+ \int p_1(y-z)^q p_1(y)^{1-q}\dd y
+ &\le C\int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta q}
+              (1+|y|)^{\beta(q-1)}\dd y\\
+ &\le C(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+       \int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta}\dd y,
+ \end{aligned}
+\]
+where \(p_1=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) and
+\(1+|y|\le(1+|z|)(1+|y-z|)\).  The final integral is finite because
+\(\beta>d\).  For the lower bound, integrate over \(|y-z|\le1\) and use
+\eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}; this gives the claimed power
+for \(|z|\ge2\).  Positivity and continuity on bounded \(z\)-sets complete
+the estimate.
+
+For \(|z|\le1\), Taylor's formula and the bounded derivative quotients give
+the pointwise bound
+\(|F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)|\le C|z|^{m+1}\), uniformly
+in \(y\).  For \(|z|>1\), \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} gives
+\(\|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_q\le C|z|^{\beta(1-1/q)}\).  The Taylor
+coefficients are bounded, so
+\(\|T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_q\le C|z|^m\).  Finally,
+\[
+ \beta(1-1/q)\le p,\qquad m\le p<m+1,
+\]
+with equality in the first relation when \(\beta>4\).  These observations
+prove \eqref{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}.
+\end{proof}

+\begin{lemma}[Stable critical translation remainder]
+\label{lem:stable-critical-translation-remainder}
+Let \(d\ge1\), \(0<\alpha<2\), \(p=p_{\alpha,d}\),
+\(q=q_{\alpha,d}\), and \(m=\lfloor p\rfloor\).  If
+\(T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)\) is the Taylor polynomial of
+\(F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\) at \(z=0\) through degree \(m\), then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth}
+ c_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+ \le \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}^q
+ \le C_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}.
+\end{equation}
+Moreover,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}
+ \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}
+ \begin{cases}
+  |z|^{m+1},&|z|\le1,\\
+  |z|^p,&|z|>1,
+ \end{cases}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}|z|^p.
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The standard stable-kernel estimates recorded as properties (G)(ii)--(iii)
+by Ishige--Kawakami--Michihisa
+\cite{IshigeKawakamiMichihisa2017} give, with constants depending on the
+chosen stable scale,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}
+ c(1+|y|)^{-\beta}\le p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)
+ \le C(1+|y|)^{-\beta},\qquad
+ |\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)|
+ \le C_\eta(1+|y|)^{-\beta-|\eta|}.
+\end{equation}
+In particular every quotient
+\(\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}/p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) is bounded.  The upper
+bound in \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} follows from
+\[
+ \begin{aligned}
+ \int p_1(y-z)^q p_1(y)^{1-q}\dd y
+ &\le C\int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta q}
+              (1+|y|)^{\beta(q-1)}\dd y\\
+ &\le C(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+       \int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta}\dd y,
+ \end{aligned}
+\]
+where \(p_1=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) and
+\(1+|y|\le(1+|z|)(1+|y-z|)\).  The final integral is finite because
+\(\beta>d\).  For the lower bound, integrate over \(|y-z|\le1\) and use
+\eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}; this gives the claimed power
+for \(|z|\ge2\).  Positivity and continuity on bounded \(z\)-sets complete
+the estimate.
+
+For \(|z|\le1\), Taylor's formula and the bounded derivative quotients give
+the pointwise bound
+\(|F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)|\le C|z|^{m+1}\), uniformly
+in \(y\).  For \(|z|>1\), \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} gives
+\(\|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_q\le C|z|^{\beta(1-1/q)}\).  The Taylor
+coefficients are bounded, so
+\(\|T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_q\le C|z|^m\).  Finally,
+\[
+ \beta(1-1/q)\le p,\qquad m\le p<m+1,
+\]
+with equality in the first relation when \(\beta>4\).  These observations
+prove \eqref{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}.
+\end{proof}

+\end{equation}
+Write \(\Omega_{\alpha,d}(\dd y)=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)\dd y\) and

+ F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)

+\begin{lemma}[Stable critical translation remainder]
+\label{lem:stable-critical-translation-remainder}
+Let \(d\ge1\), \(0<\alpha<2\), \(p=p_{\alpha,d}\),
+\(q=q_{\alpha,d}\), and \(m=\lfloor p\rfloor\).  If
+\(T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)\) is the Taylor polynomial of
+\(F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\) at \(z=0\) through degree \(m\), then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth}
+ c_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+ \le \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}^q
+ \le C_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}.
+\end{equation}
+Moreover,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}
+ \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}
+ \begin{cases}
+  |z|^{m+1},&|z|\le1,\\
+  |z|^p,&|z|>1,
+ \end{cases}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}|z|^p.
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The standard stable-kernel estimates recorded as properties (G)(ii)--(iii)
+by Ishige--Kawakami--Michihisa
+\cite{IshigeKawakamiMichihisa2017} give, with constants depending on the
+chosen stable scale,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}
+ c(1+|y|)^{-\beta}\le p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)
+ \le C(1+|y|)^{-\beta},\qquad
+ |\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)|
+ \le C_\eta(1+|y|)^{-\beta-|\eta|}.
+\end{equation}
+In particular every quotient
+\(\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}/p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) is bounded.  The upper
+bound in \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} follows from
+\[
+ \begin{aligned}
+ \int p_1(y-z)^q p_1(y)^{1-q}\dd y
+ &\le C\int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta q}
+              (1+|y|)^{\beta(q-1)}\dd y\\
+ &\le C(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+       \int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta}\dd y,
+ \end{aligned}
+\]
+where \(p_1=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) and
+\(1+|y|\le(1+|z|)(1+|y-z|)\).  The final integral is finite because
+\(\beta>d\).  For the lower bound, integrate over \(|y-z|\le1\) and use
+\eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}; this gives the claimed power
+for \(|z|\ge2\).  Positivity and continuity on bounded \(z\)-sets complete
+the estimate.
+
+For \(|z|\le1\), Taylor's formula and the bounded derivative quotients give
+the pointwise bound
+\(|F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)|\le C|z|^{m+1}\), uniformly
+in \(y\).  For \(|z|>1\), \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} gives
+\(\|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_q\le C|z|^{\beta(1-1/q)}\).  The Taylor
+coefficients are bounded, so
+\(\|T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_q\le C|z|^m\).  Finally,
+\[
+ \beta(1-1/q)\le p,\qquad m\le p<m+1,
+\]
+with equality in the first relation when \(\beta>4\).  These observations
+prove \eqref{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}.
+\end{proof}

+\begin{lemma}[Stable critical translation remainder]
+\label{lem:stable-critical-translation-remainder}
+Let \(d\ge1\), \(0<\alpha<2\), \(p=p_{\alpha,d}\),
+\(q=q_{\alpha,d}\), and \(m=\lfloor p\rfloor\).  If
+\(T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)\) is the Taylor polynomial of
+\(F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\) at \(z=0\) through degree \(m\), then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth}
+ c_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+ \le \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}^q
+ \le C_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}.
+\end{equation}
+Moreover,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}
+ \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}
+ \begin{cases}
+  |z|^{m+1},&|z|\le1,\\
+  |z|^p,&|z|>1,
+ \end{cases}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}|z|^p.
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The standard stable-kernel estimates recorded as properties (G)(ii)--(iii)
+by Ishige--Kawakami--Michihisa
+\cite{IshigeKawakamiMichihisa2017} give, with constants depending on the
+chosen stable scale,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}
+ c(1+|y|)^{-\beta}\le p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)
+ \le C(1+|y|)^{-\beta},\qquad
+ |\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)|

+\end{equation}
+In particular every quotient

+\[

+              (1+|y|)^{\beta(q-1)}\dd y\\

+ \end{aligned}
+\]
+where \(p_1=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) and
+\(1+|y|\le(1+|z|)(1+|y-z|)\).  The final integral is finite because
+\(\beta>d\).  For the lower bound, integrate over \(|y-z|\le1\) and use
+\eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}; this gives the claimed power
+for \(|z|\ge2\).  Positivity and continuity on bounded \(z\)-sets complete
+the estimate.
+
+For \(|z|\le1\), Taylor's formula and the bounded derivative quotients give
+the pointwise bound
+\(|F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)|\le C|z|^{m+1}\), uniformly
+in \(y\).  For \(|z|>1\), \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} gives
+\(\|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_q\le C|z|^{\beta(1-1/q)}\).  The Taylor
+coefficients are bounded, so
+\(\|T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_q\le C|z|^m\).  Finally,
+\[
+ \beta(1-1/q)\le p,\qquad m\le p<m+1,
+\]
+with equality in the first relation when \(\beta>4\).  These observations
+prove \eqref{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}.
+\end{proof}

# Verification Before Completion

## Overview

Claiming work is complete without verification is dishonesty, not efficiency.

**Core principle:** Evidence before claims, always.

**Violating the letter of this rule is violating the spirit of this rule.**

## The Iron Law

```
NO COMPLETION CLAIMS WITHOUT FRESH VERIFICATION EVIDENCE
```

If you haven't run the verification command in this message, you cannot claim it passes.

## The Gate Function

```
BEFORE claiming any status or expressing satisfaction:

1. IDENTIFY: What command proves this claim?
2. RUN: Execute the FULL command (fresh, complete)
3. READ: Full output, check exit code, count failures
4. VERIFY: Does output confirm the claim?
   - If NO: State actual status with evidence
   - If YES: State claim WITH evidence
5. ONLY THEN: Make the claim

Skip any step = lying, not verifying
```

## Common Failures

| Claim | Requires | Not Sufficient |
|-------|----------|----------------|
| Tests pass | Test command output: 0 failures | Previous run, "should pass" |
| Linter clean | Linter output: 0 errors | Partial check, extrapolation |
| Build succeeds | Build command: exit 0 | Linter passing, logs look good |
| Bug fixed | Test original symptom: passes | Code changed, assumed fixed |
| Regression test works | Red-green cycle verified | Test passes once |
| Agent completed | VCS diff shows changes | Agent reports "success" |
| Requirements met | Line-by-line checklist | Tests passing |

## Red Flags - STOP

- Using "should", "probably", "seems to"
- Expressing satisfaction before verification ("Great!", "Perfect!", "Done!", etc.)
- About to commit/push/PR without verification
- Trusting agent success reports
- Relying on partial verification
- Thinking "just this once"
- Tired and wanting work over
- **ANY wording implying success without having run verification**

## Rationalization Prevention

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Should work now" | RUN the verification |
| "I'm confident" | Confidence â‰  evidence |
| "Just this once" | No exceptions |
| "Linter passed" | Linter â‰  compiler |
| "Agent said success" | Verify independently |
| "I'm tired" | Exhaustion â‰  excuse |
| "Partial check is enough" | Partial proves nothing |
| "Different words so rule doesn't apply" | Spirit over letter |

## Key Patterns

**Tests:**
```
âœ… [Run test command] [See: 34/34 pass] "All tests pass"
âŒ "Should pass now" / "Looks correct"
```

**Regression tests (TDD Red-Green):**
```
âœ… Write â†’ Run (pass) â†’ Revert fix â†’ Run (MUST FAIL) â†’ Restore â†’ Run (pass)
âŒ "I've written a regression test" (without red-green verification)
```

**Build:**
```
âœ… [Run build] [See: exit 0] "Build passes"
âŒ "Linter passed" (linter doesn't check compilation)
```

**Requirements:**
```
âœ… Re-read plan â†’ Create checklist â†’ Verify each â†’ Report gaps or completion
âŒ "Tests pass, phase complete"
```

**Agent delegation:**
```
âœ… Agent reports success â†’ Check VCS diff â†’ Verify changes â†’ Report actual state
âŒ Trust agent report
```

## Why This Matters

From 24 failure memories:
- your human partner said "I don't believe you" - trust broken
- Undefined functions shipped - would crash
- Missing requirements shipped - incomplete features
- Time wasted on false completion â†’ redirect â†’ rework
- Violates: "Honesty is a core value. If you lie, you'll be replaced."

## When To Apply

**ALWAYS before:**
- ANY variation of success/completion claims
- ANY expression of satisfaction
- ANY positive statement about work state
- Committing, PR creation, task completion
- Moving to next task
- Delegating to agents

**Rule applies to:**
- Exact phrases
- Paraphrases and synonyms
- Implications of success
- ANY communication suggesting completion/correctness

## The Bottom Line

**No shortcuts for verification.**

Run the command. Read the output. THEN claim the result.

This is non-negotiable.

+\begin{lemma}[Stable critical translation remainder]
+\label{lem:stable-critical-translation-remainder}
+Let \(d\ge1\), \(0<\alpha<2\), \(p=p_{\alpha,d}\),
+\(q=q_{\alpha,d}\), and \(m=\lfloor p\rfloor\).  If
+\(T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)\) is the Taylor polynomial of
+\(F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\) at \(z=0\) through degree \(m\), then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth}
+ c_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+ \le \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}^q
+ \le C_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}.
+\end{equation}
+Moreover,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}
+ \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}
+ \begin{cases}
+  |z|^{m+1},&|z|\le1,\\
+  |z|^p,&|z|>1,
+ \end{cases}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}|z|^p.
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The standard stable-kernel estimates recorded as properties (G)(ii)--(iii)
+by Ishige--Kawakami--Michihisa
+\cite{IshigeKawakamiMichihisa2017} give, with constants depending on the
+chosen stable scale,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}
+ c(1+|y|)^{-\beta}\le p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)
+ \le C(1+|y|)^{-\beta},\qquad
+ |\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)|
+ \le C_\eta(1+|y|)^{-\beta-|\eta|}.
+\end{equation}
+In particular every quotient
+\(\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}/p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) is bounded.  The upper
+bound in \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} follows from
+\[
+ \begin{aligned}
+ \int p_1(y-z)^q p_1(y)^{1-q}\dd y
+ &\le C\int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta q}
+              (1+|y|)^{\beta(q-1)}\dd y\\
+ &\le C(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+       \int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta}\dd y,
+ \end{aligned}
+\]
+where \(p_1=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) and
+\(1+|y|\le(1+|z|)(1+|y-z|)\).  The final integral is finite because
+\(\beta>d\).  For the lower bound, integrate over \(|y-z|\le1\) and use
+\eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}; this gives the claimed power
+for \(|z|\ge2\).  Positivity and continuity on bounded \(z\)-sets complete
+the estimate.
+
+For \(|z|\le1\), Taylor's formula and the bounded derivative quotients give
+the pointwise bound
+\(|F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)|\le C|z|^{m+1}\), uniformly
+in \(y\).  For \(|z|>1\), \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} gives
+\(\|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_q\le C|z|^{\beta(1-1/q)}\).  The Taylor
+coefficients are bounded, so
+\(\|T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_q\le C|z|^m\).  Finally,
+\[
+ \beta(1-1/q)\le p,\qquad m\le p<m+1,
+\]
+with equality in the first relation when \(\beta>4\).  These observations
+prove \eqref{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}.
+\end{proof}

+For \(0<\alpha<2\), let \(p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) be the density of any
+centred isotropic strictly \(\alpha\)-stable law on \(\RR^d\), and use the
+spatial-scale normalization
+\[
+ p_s^{(\alpha,d)}(x)=s^{-d}p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(x/s),\qquad s>0.
+\]
+Changing the scale parameter in the characteristic exponent only changes
+the choice of \(p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\), so this notation covers every isotropic
+strictly stable kernel.  Put
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-critical-exponents}
+ \beta=d+\alpha,\qquad
+ q_{\alpha,d}:=\min\left\{2,1+\frac4\beta\right\},\qquad
+ p_{\alpha,d}:=\frac4{q_{\alpha,d}}
+ =\max\left\{2,\frac{4(d+\alpha)}{d+\alpha+4}\right\}.
+\end{equation}
+Write \(\Omega_{\alpha,d}(\dd y)=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)\dd y\) and
+\[
+ F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)
+ :=\frac{p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y-z)}{p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)}.

+\begin{lemma}[Stable critical translation remainder]
+\label{lem:stable-critical-translation-remainder}
+Let \(d\ge1\), \(0<\alpha<2\), \(p=p_{\alpha,d}\),
+\(q=q_{\alpha,d}\), and \(m=\lfloor p\rfloor\).  If
+\(T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)\) is the Taylor polynomial of
+\(F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\) at \(z=0\) through degree \(m\), then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth}
+ c_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+ \le \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}^q
+ \le C_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}.
+\end{equation}
+Moreover,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}
+ \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}
+ \begin{cases}
+  |z|^{m+1},&|z|\le1,\\
+  |z|^p,&|z|>1,
+ \end{cases}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}|z|^p.
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The standard stable-kernel estimates recorded as properties (G)(ii)--(iii)
+by Ishige--Kawakami--Michihisa
+\cite{IshigeKawakamiMichihisa2017} give, with constants depending on the
+chosen stable scale,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}
+ c(1+|y|)^{-\beta}\le p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)
+ \le C(1+|y|)^{-\beta},\qquad
+ |\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)|
+ \le C_\eta(1+|y|)^{-\beta-|\eta|}.
+\end{equation}
+In particular every quotient
+\(\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}/p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) is bounded.  The upper
+bound in \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} follows from
+\[
+ \begin{aligned}
+ \int p_1(y-z)^q p_1(y)^{1-q}\dd y
+ &\le C\int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta q}
+              (1+|y|)^{\beta(q-1)}\dd y\\
+ &\le C(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+       \int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta}\dd y,
+ \end{aligned}
+\]
+where \(p_1=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) and
+\(1+|y|\le(1+|z|)(1+|y-z|)\).  The final integral is finite because
+\(\beta>d\).  For the lower bound, integrate over \(|y-z|\le1\) and use
+\eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}; this gives the claimed power
+for \(|z|\ge2\).  Positivity and continuity on bounded \(z\)-sets complete
+the estimate.
+
+For \(|z|\le1\), Taylor's formula and the bounded derivative quotients give
+the pointwise bound
+\(|F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)|\le C|z|^{m+1}\), uniformly
+in \(y\).  For \(|z|>1\), \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} gives
+\(\|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_q\le C|z|^{\beta(1-1/q)}\).  The Taylor
+coefficients are bounded, so
+\(\|T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_q\le C|z|^m\).  Finally,
+\[
+ \beta(1-1/q)\le p,\qquad m\le p<m+1,
+\]
+with equality in the first relation when \(\beta>4\).  These observations
+prove \eqref{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}.
+\end{proof}

+For \(0<\alpha<2\), let \(p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) be the density of any
+centred isotropic strictly \(\alpha\)-stable law on \(\RR^d\), and use the
+spatial-scale normalization
+\[
+ p_s^{(\alpha,d)}(x)=s^{-d}p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(x/s),\qquad s>0.
+\]
+Changing the scale parameter in the characteristic exponent only changes
+the choice of \(p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\), so this notation covers every isotropic
+strictly stable kernel.  Put
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-critical-exponents}
+ \beta=d+\alpha,\qquad
+ q_{\alpha,d}:=\min\left\{2,1+\frac4\beta\right\},\qquad
+ p_{\alpha,d}:=\frac4{q_{\alpha,d}}
+ =\max\left\{2,\frac{4(d+\alpha)}{d+\alpha+4}\right\}.
+\end{equation}
+Write \(\Omega_{\alpha,d}(\dd y)=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)\dd y\) and
+\[
+ F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)
+ :=\frac{p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y-z)}{p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)}.

+\begin{lemma}[Stable critical translation remainder]
+\label{lem:stable-critical-translation-remainder}
+Let \(d\ge1\), \(0<\alpha<2\), \(p=p_{\alpha,d}\),
+\(q=q_{\alpha,d}\), and \(m=\lfloor p\rfloor\).  If
+\(T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)\) is the Taylor polynomial of
+\(F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\) at \(z=0\) through degree \(m\), then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth}
+ c_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+ \le \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}^q
+ \le C_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}.
+\end{equation}
+Moreover,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}
+ \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}
+ \begin{cases}
+  |z|^{m+1},&|z|\le1,\\
+  |z|^p,&|z|>1,
+ \end{cases}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}|z|^p.
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The standard stable-kernel estimates recorded as properties (G)(ii)--(iii)
+by Ishige--Kawakami--Michihisa
+\cite{IshigeKawakamiMichihisa2017} give, with constants depending on the
+chosen stable scale,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}
+ c(1+|y|)^{-\beta}\le p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)
+ \le C(1+|y|)^{-\beta},\qquad
+ |\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)|
+ \le C_\eta(1+|y|)^{-\beta-|\eta|}.
+\end{equation}
+In particular every quotient
+\(\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}/p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) is bounded.  The upper
+bound in \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} follows from
+\[
+ \begin{aligned}
+ \int p_1(y-z)^q p_1(y)^{1-q}\dd y
+ &\le C\int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta q}
+              (1+|y|)^{\beta(q-1)}\dd y\\
+ &\le C(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+       \int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta}\dd y,
+ \end{aligned}
+\]
+where \(p_1=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) and
+\(1+|y|\le(1+|z|)(1+|y-z|)\).  The final integral is finite because
+\(\beta>d\).  For the lower bound, integrate over \(|y-z|\le1\) and use
+\eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}; this gives the claimed power
+for \(|z|\ge2\).  Positivity and continuity on bounded \(z\)-sets complete
+the estimate.
+
+For \(|z|\le1\), Taylor's formula and the bounded derivative quotients give
+the pointwise bound
+\(|F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)|\le C|z|^{m+1}\), uniformly
+in \(y\).  For \(|z|>1\), \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} gives
+\(\|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_q\le C|z|^{\beta(1-1/q)}\).  The Taylor
+coefficients are bounded, so
+\(\|T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_q\le C|z|^m\).  Finally,
+\[
+ \beta(1-1/q)\le p,\qquad m\le p<m+1,
+\]
+with equality in the first relation when \(\beta>4\).  These observations
+prove \eqref{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}.
+\end{proof}

+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth}
+ c_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+ \le \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}^q
+ \le C_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}.
+\end{equation}
+Moreover,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}
+ \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}
+ \begin{cases}
+  |z|^{m+1},&|z|\le1,\\
+  |z|^p,&|z|>1,
+ \end{cases}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}|z|^p.
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The standard stable-kernel estimates recorded as properties (G)(ii)--(iii)
+by Ishige--Kawakami--Michihisa
+\cite{IshigeKawakamiMichihisa2017} give, with constants depending on the
+chosen stable scale,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}
+ c(1+|y|)^{-\beta}\le p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)
+ \le C(1+|y|)^{-\beta},\qquad
+ |\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)|
+ \le C_\eta(1+|y|)^{-\beta-|\eta|}.
+\end{equation}
+In particular every quotient
+\(\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}/p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) is bounded.  The upper
+bound in \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} follows from
+\[
+ \begin{aligned}
+ \int p_1(y-z)^q p_1(y)^{1-q}\dd y
+ &\le C\int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta q}
+              (1+|y|)^{\beta(q-1)}\dd y\\
+ &\le C(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+       \int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta}\dd y,
+ \end{aligned}
+\]
+where \(p_1=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) and
+\(1+|y|\le(1+|z|)(1+|y-z|)\).  The final integral is finite because
+\(\beta>d\).  For the lower bound, integrate over \(|y-z|\le1\) and use
+\eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}; this gives the claimed power
+for \(|z|\ge2\).  Positivity and continuity on bounded \(z\)-sets complete
+the estimate.
+
+For \(|z|\le1\), Taylor's formula and the bounded derivative quotients give
+the pointwise bound
+\(|F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)|\le C|z|^{m+1}\), uniformly
+in \(y\).  For \(|z|>1\), \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} gives
+\(\|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_q\le C|z|^{\beta(1-1/q)}\).  The Taylor
+coefficients are bounded, so
+\(\|T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_q\le C|z|^m\).  Finally,
+\[
+ \beta(1-1/q)\le p,\qquad m\le p<m+1,
+\]
+with equality in the first relation when \(\beta>4\).  These observations
+prove \eqref{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}.
+\end{proof}

+Write \(\Omega_{\alpha,d}(\dd y)=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)\dd y\) and

+\begin{lemma}[Stable critical translation remainder]
+\label{lem:stable-critical-translation-remainder}
+Let \(d\ge1\), \(0<\alpha<2\), \(p=p_{\alpha,d}\),
+\(q=q_{\alpha,d}\), and \(m=\lfloor p\rfloor\).  If
+\(T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)\) is the Taylor polynomial of
+\(F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\) at \(z=0\) through degree \(m\), then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth}
+ c_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+ \le \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}^q
+ \le C_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}.
+\end{equation}
+Moreover,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}
+ \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}
+ \begin{cases}
+  |z|^{m+1},&|z|\le1,\\
+  |z|^p,&|z|>1,
+ \end{cases}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}|z|^p.
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The standard stable-kernel estimates recorded as properties (G)(ii)--(iii)
+by Ishige--Kawakami--Michihisa
+\cite{IshigeKawakamiMichihisa2017} give, with constants depending on the
+chosen stable scale,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}
+ c(1+|y|)^{-\beta}\le p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)
+ \le C(1+|y|)^{-\beta},\qquad
+ |\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)|
+ \le C_\eta(1+|y|)^{-\beta-|\eta|}.
+\end{equation}
+In particular every quotient
+\(\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}/p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) is bounded.  The upper
+bound in \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} follows from
+\[
+ \begin{aligned}
+ \int p_1(y-z)^q p_1(y)^{1-q}\dd y
+ &\le C\int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta q}
+              (1+|y|)^{\beta(q-1)}\dd y\\
+ &\le C(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+       \int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta}\dd y,
+ \end{aligned}
+\]
+where \(p_1=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) and
+\(1+|y|\le(1+|z|)(1+|y-z|)\).  The final integral is finite because
+\(\beta>d\).  For the lower bound, integrate over \(|y-z|\le1\) and use
+\eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}; this gives the claimed power
+for \(|z|\ge2\).  Positivity and continuity on bounded \(z\)-sets complete
+the estimate.
+
+For \(|z|\le1\), Taylor's formula and the bounded derivative quotients give
+the pointwise bound
+\(|F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)|\le C|z|^{m+1}\), uniformly
+in \(y\).  For \(|z|>1\), \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} gives
+\(\|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_q\le C|z|^{\beta(1-1/q)}\).  The Taylor
+coefficients are bounded, so
+\(\|T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_q\le C|z|^m\).  Finally,
+\[
+ \beta(1-1/q)\le p,\qquad m\le p<m+1,
+\]
+with equality in the first relation when \(\beta>4\).  These observations
+prove \eqref{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}.
+\end{proof}

 \eqref{eq:critical-kl-quotient-decomposition},
 \[
- \int\Phi(u_t)\dd\Omega_d
- =\frac{t^{-4}}2\int b_\Sigma^2\dd\Omega_d+o(t^{-4})
- =\mathcal Q_d(\Sigma)t^{-4}+o(t^{-4}),
+ \int\Phi(u_s)\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+ =\frac{s^{-4}}2\int b_{\alpha,d,\Sigma}^2\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+   +o(s^{-4})
+ =\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d}(\Sigma)s^{-4}+o(s^{-4}),
 \]
 which proves \eqref{eq:critical-kl-leading-asymptotic}.
 
-For sharpness, fix \(2\le r<p_d\) and repeat the symmetric spike
-construction in the proof of
-Proposition~\ref{prop:high-dimensional-finite-covariance-obstruction} with
-\(w_j=\alpha_jR_j^{-r}\), where \(\sum_j\alpha_j<\infty\).  At
-\(t_j=\kappa R_jw_j^{1/(d+1)}\), the same binary data-processing estimate
-gives
+We first prove the obstruction below two moments.  If
+\(\limsup_{s\to\infty}s^4H_{\alpha,d}(s)<\infty\), Pinsker's inequality
+and scaling give, for every fixed \(\xi\in\RR^d\),
+\[
+ |\widehat p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(\xi)|
+ |\varphi_X(\xi/s)-1|
+ \le \|p_1^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu_s-p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\|_1
+ \le \sqrt{2H_{\alpha,d}(s)}=O(s^{-2}),
+\]
+where \(\nu_s\) is the law of \(X/s\).  Since the stable characteristic
+function never vanishes, take \(\xi=e\) for a unit vector \(e\), multiply
+the real part by \(s^2\), and use Fatou's lemma to obtain
+\[
+ \frac12\EE(e\cdot X)^2
+ \le \liminf_{s\to\infty}s^2
+       \EE[1-\cos((e\cdot X)/s)]<\infty.
+\]
+Thus bounded scaled entropy forces finite covariance.  Given \(0<r<2\),
+choose \(a\in(\max\{1,r\},2)\) and put symmetric masses proportional to
+\(n^{-a-1}\) at \(\pm ne_1\), with the remaining mass at zero.  This law
+has mean zero and finite \(r\)th moment but infinite variance, so its scaled
+entropy has infinite limsup.
+
+It remains to prove optimality between two and \(p\) when \(\beta>4\).
+Fix \(2\le r<p\), choose positive \(a_j\) with \(\sum_ja_j<\infty\), and
+put symmetric masses \(w_j/2\) at \(\pm R_je_1\), where
+\(w_j=a_jR_j^{-r}\).  Add a sufficiently small bounded symmetric spanning
+component.  The resulting law has positive-definite finite covariance and
+finite \(r\)th moment.  Set
+\[
+ s_j=\kappa R_jw_j^{1/\beta},\qquad
+ A_j=B(R_je_1,s_j).
+\]
+The component at \(R_je_1\) gives
+\((p_{s_j}^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu)(A_j)\ge c_{\alpha,d}w_j\).  On the other hand,
+\eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds} and \(s_j/R_j\to0\) give
+\[
+ p_{s_j}^{(\alpha,d)}(A_j)
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}(s_j/R_j)^\beta
+ =C_{\alpha,d}\kappa^\beta w_j.
+\]
+Choose \(\kappa\) so that the second Bernoulli mass is a fixed small
+fraction of the first.  Data processing to
+\(\{A_j,A_j^c\}\) then yields \(H_{\alpha,d}(s_j)\ge c w_j\), and hence
 \[
- t_j^4H_d(t_j)\ge c_dR_j^4w_j^{1+4/(d+1)}
- =c_d\alpha_j^{q_d}R_j^{4-rq_d}.
+ s_j^4H_{\alpha,d}(s_j)
+ \ge cR_j^4w_j^{1+4/\beta}
+ =ca_j^{q_{\alpha,d}}R_j^{4-rq_{\alpha,d}}.
 \]
-Since \(r<p_d=4/q_d\), the exponent of \(R_j\) is positive.  Recursive
-choice of the radii makes this expression unbounded while preserving the
-finite \(r\)th moment and, after adding a bounded spanning component, a
-positive-definite covariance.
+Here \(q_{\alpha,d}=1+4/\beta\) and
+\(r<p=4/q_{\alpha,d}\), so the exponent of \(R_j\) is positive.
+Recursive choice of the radii makes \(s_j\to\infty\) and the last display
+unbounded while preserving all moment assertions.
 \end{proof}

+Write \(\Omega_{\alpha,d}(\dd y)=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)\dd y\) and

+\begin{lemma}[Stable critical translation remainder]
+\label{lem:stable-critical-translation-remainder}
+Let \(d\ge1\), \(0<\alpha<2\), \(p=p_{\alpha,d}\),
+\(q=q_{\alpha,d}\), and \(m=\lfloor p\rfloor\).  If
+\(T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)\) is the Taylor polynomial of
+\(F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\) at \(z=0\) through degree \(m\), then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth}
+ c_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+ \le \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}^q
+ \le C_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}.
+\end{equation}
+Moreover,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}
+ \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}
+ \begin{cases}
+  |z|^{m+1},&|z|\le1,\\
+  |z|^p,&|z|>1,
+ \end{cases}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}|z|^p.
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The standard stable-kernel estimates recorded as properties (G)(ii)--(iii)
+by Ishige--Kawakami--Michihisa
+\cite{IshigeKawakamiMichihisa2017} give, with constants depending on the
+chosen stable scale,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}
+ c(1+|y|)^{-\beta}\le p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)
+ \le C(1+|y|)^{-\beta},\qquad
+ |\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)|
+ \le C_\eta(1+|y|)^{-\beta-|\eta|}.
+\end{equation}
+In particular every quotient
+\(\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}/p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) is bounded.  The upper
+bound in \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} follows from
+\[
+ \begin{aligned}
+ \int p_1(y-z)^q p_1(y)^{1-q}\dd y
+ &\le C\int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta q}
+              (1+|y|)^{\beta(q-1)}\dd y\\
+ &\le C(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+       \int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta}\dd y,
+ \end{aligned}
+\]
+where \(p_1=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) and
+\(1+|y|\le(1+|z|)(1+|y-z|)\).  The final integral is finite because
+\(\beta>d\).  For the lower bound, integrate over \(|y-z|\le1\) and use
+\eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}; this gives the claimed power
+for \(|z|\ge2\).  Positivity and continuity on bounded \(z\)-sets complete
+the estimate.
+
+For \(|z|\le1\), Taylor's formula and the bounded derivative quotients give
+the pointwise bound
+\(|F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)|\le C|z|^{m+1}\), uniformly
+in \(y\).  For \(|z|>1\), \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} gives
+\(\|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_q\le C|z|^{\beta(1-1/q)}\).  The Taylor
+coefficients are bounded, so
+\(\|T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_q\le C|z|^m\).  Finally,
+\[
+ \beta(1-1/q)\le p,\qquad m\le p<m+1,
+\]
+with equality in the first relation when \(\beta>4\).  These observations
+prove \eqref{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}.
+\end{proof}

+\]

 \end{proof}

+ \beta=d+\alpha,\qquad
+ q_{\alpha,d}:=\min\left\{2,1+\frac4\beta\right\},\qquad

+\end{equation}
+Write \(\Omega_{\alpha,d}(\dd y)=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)\dd y\) and
+\[
+ F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)
+ :=\frac{p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y-z)}{p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)}.
+\]

+\begin{lemma}[Stable critical translation remainder]
+\label{lem:stable-critical-translation-remainder}
+Let \(d\ge1\), \(0<\alpha<2\), \(p=p_{\alpha,d}\),
+\(q=q_{\alpha,d}\), and \(m=\lfloor p\rfloor\).  If
+\(T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)\) is the Taylor polynomial of
+\(F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\) at \(z=0\) through degree \(m\), then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth}
+ c_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+ \le \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}^q
+ \le C_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}.
+\end{equation}
+Moreover,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}
+ \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}
+ \begin{cases}
+  |z|^{m+1},&|z|\le1,\\
+  |z|^p,&|z|>1,
+ \end{cases}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}|z|^p.
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The standard stable-kernel estimates recorded as properties (G)(ii)--(iii)
+by Ishige--Kawakami--Michihisa
+\cite{IshigeKawakamiMichihisa2017} give, with constants depending on the
+chosen stable scale,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}
+ c(1+|y|)^{-\beta}\le p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)
+ \le C(1+|y|)^{-\beta},\qquad
+ |\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)|
+ \le C_\eta(1+|y|)^{-\beta-|\eta|}.
+\end{equation}
+In particular every quotient
+\(\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}/p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) is bounded.  The upper
+bound in \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} follows from
+\[
+ \begin{aligned}
+ \int p_1(y-z)^q p_1(y)^{1-q}\dd y
+ &\le C\int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta q}
+              (1+|y|)^{\beta(q-1)}\dd y\\
+ &\le C(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+       \int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta}\dd y,
+ \end{aligned}
+\]
+where \(p_1=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) and
+\(1+|y|\le(1+|z|)(1+|y-z|)\).  The final integral is finite because
+\(\beta>d\).  For the lower bound, integrate over \(|y-z|\le1\) and use
+\eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}; this gives the claimed power
+for \(|z|\ge2\).  Positivity and continuity on bounded \(z\)-sets complete
+the estimate.
+
+For \(|z|\le1\), Taylor's formula and the bounded derivative quotients give
+the pointwise bound
+\(|F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)|\le C|z|^{m+1}\), uniformly
+in \(y\).  For \(|z|>1\), \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} gives
+\(\|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_q\le C|z|^{\beta(1-1/q)}\).  The Taylor
+coefficients are bounded, so
+\(\|T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_q\le C|z|^m\).  Finally,
+\[

+\end{equation}
+Write \(\Omega_{\alpha,d}(\dd y)=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)\dd y\) and

+\begin{lemma}[Stable critical translation remainder]
+\label{lem:stable-critical-translation-remainder}
+Let \(d\ge1\), \(0<\alpha<2\), \(p=p_{\alpha,d}\),
+\(q=q_{\alpha,d}\), and \(m=\lfloor p\rfloor\).  If
+\(T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)\) is the Taylor polynomial of
+\(F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\) at \(z=0\) through degree \(m\), then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth}
+ c_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+ \le \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}^q
+ \le C_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}.
+\end{equation}
+Moreover,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}
+ \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}
+ \begin{cases}
+  |z|^{m+1},&|z|\le1,\\
+  |z|^p,&|z|>1,
+ \end{cases}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}|z|^p.
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The standard stable-kernel estimates recorded as properties (G)(ii)--(iii)
+by Ishige--Kawakami--Michihisa
+\cite{IshigeKawakamiMichihisa2017} give, with constants depending on the
+chosen stable scale,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}
+ c(1+|y|)^{-\beta}\le p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)
+ \le C(1+|y|)^{-\beta},\qquad
+ |\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)|
+ \le C_\eta(1+|y|)^{-\beta-|\eta|}.
+\end{equation}
+In particular every quotient
+\(\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}/p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) is bounded.  The upper
+bound in \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} follows from
+\[
+ \begin{aligned}
+ \int p_1(y-z)^q p_1(y)^{1-q}\dd y
+ &\le C\int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta q}
+              (1+|y|)^{\beta(q-1)}\dd y\\
+ &\le C(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+       \int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta}\dd y,
+ \end{aligned}
+\]
+where \(p_1=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) and
+\(1+|y|\le(1+|z|)(1+|y-z|)\).  The final integral is finite because
+\(\beta>d\).  For the lower bound, integrate over \(|y-z|\le1\) and use
+\eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}; this gives the claimed power
+for \(|z|\ge2\).  Positivity and continuity on bounded \(z\)-sets complete
+the estimate.
+
+For \(|z|\le1\), Taylor's formula and the bounded derivative quotients give
+the pointwise bound
+\(|F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)|\le C|z|^{m+1}\), uniformly
+in \(y\).  For \(|z|>1\), \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} gives
+\(\|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_q\le C|z|^{\beta(1-1/q)}\).  The Taylor
+coefficients are bounded, so
+\(\|T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_q\le C|z|^m\).  Finally,
+\[
+ \beta(1-1/q)\le p,\qquad m\le p<m+1,
+\]
+with equality in the first relation when \(\beta>4\).  These observations
+prove \eqref{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}.
+\end{proof}

+ \le C_{\alpha,d}(s_j/R_j)^\beta
+ =C_{\alpha,d}\kappa^\beta w_j.
+\]
+Choose \(\kappa\) so that the second Bernoulli mass is a fixed small
+fraction of the first.  Data processing to
+\(\{A_j,A_j^c\}\) then yields \(H_{\alpha,d}(s_j)\ge c w_j\), and hence
 \[
- t_j^4H_d(t_j)\ge c_dR_j^4w_j^{1+4/(d+1)}
- =c_d\alpha_j^{q_d}R_j^{4-rq_d}.
+ s_j^4H_{\alpha,d}(s_j)
+ \ge cR_j^4w_j^{1+4/\beta}
+ =ca_j^{q_{\alpha,d}}R_j^{4-rq_{\alpha,d}}.
 \]
-Since \(r<p_d=4/q_d\), the exponent of \(R_j\) is positive.  Recursive
-choice of the radii makes this expression unbounded while preserving the
-finite \(r\)th moment and, after adding a bounded spanning component, a
-positive-definite covariance.
+Here \(q_{\alpha,d}=1+4/\beta\) and
+\(r<p=4/q_{\alpha,d}\), so the exponent of \(R_j\) is positive.
+Recursive choice of the radii makes \(s_j\to\infty\) and the last display
+unbounded while preserving all moment assertions.
 \end{proof}

+For \(0<\alpha<2\), let \(p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) be the density of any

+\end{equation}
+Write \(\Omega_{\alpha,d}(\dd y)=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)\dd y\) and

+\begin{lemma}[Stable critical translation remainder]
+\label{lem:stable-critical-translation-remainder}
+Let \(d\ge1\), \(0<\alpha<2\), \(p=p_{\alpha,d}\),
+\(q=q_{\alpha,d}\), and \(m=\lfloor p\rfloor\).  If
+\(T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)\) is the Taylor polynomial of
+\(F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\) at \(z=0\) through degree \(m\), then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth}
+ c_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+ \le \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}^q
+ \le C_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}.
+\end{equation}
+Moreover,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}
+ \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}
+ \begin{cases}
+  |z|^{m+1},&|z|\le1,\\
+  |z|^p,&|z|>1,
+ \end{cases}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}|z|^p.
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The standard stable-kernel estimates recorded as properties (G)(ii)--(iii)
+by Ishige--Kawakami--Michihisa
+\cite{IshigeKawakamiMichihisa2017} give, with constants depending on the
+chosen stable scale,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}
+ c(1+|y|)^{-\beta}\le p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)
+ \le C(1+|y|)^{-\beta},\qquad
+ |\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)|
+ \le C_\eta(1+|y|)^{-\beta-|\eta|}.
+\end{equation}
+In particular every quotient
+\(\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}/p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) is bounded.  The upper
+bound in \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} follows from
+\[
+ \begin{aligned}
+ \int p_1(y-z)^q p_1(y)^{1-q}\dd y
+ &\le C\int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta q}
+              (1+|y|)^{\beta(q-1)}\dd y\\
+ &\le C(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+       \int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta}\dd y,
+ \end{aligned}
+\]
+where \(p_1=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) and
+\(1+|y|\le(1+|z|)(1+|y-z|)\).  The final integral is finite because
+\(\beta>d\).  For the lower bound, integrate over \(|y-z|\le1\) and use
+\eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}; this gives the claimed power
+for \(|z|\ge2\).  Positivity and continuity on bounded \(z\)-sets complete
+the estimate.
+
+For \(|z|\le1\), Taylor's formula and the bounded derivative quotients give
+the pointwise bound
+\(|F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)|\le C|z|^{m+1}\), uniformly
+in \(y\).  For \(|z|>1\), \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} gives
+\(\|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_q\le C|z|^{\beta(1-1/q)}\).  The Taylor
+coefficients are bounded, so
+\(\|T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_q\le C|z|^m\).  Finally,
+\[
+ \beta(1-1/q)\le p,\qquad m\le p<m+1,
+\]
+with equality in the first relation when \(\beta>4\).  These observations
+prove \eqref{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}.
+\end{proof}

+\begin{lemma}[Stable critical translation remainder]
+\label{lem:stable-critical-translation-remainder}
+Let \(d\ge1\), \(0<\alpha<2\), \(p=p_{\alpha,d}\),
+\(q=q_{\alpha,d}\), and \(m=\lfloor p\rfloor\).  If
+\(T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)\) is the Taylor polynomial of
+\(F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\) at \(z=0\) through degree \(m\), then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth}
+ c_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+ \le \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}^q
+ \le C_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}.
+\end{equation}
+Moreover,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}
+ \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}
+ \begin{cases}
+  |z|^{m+1},&|z|\le1,\\
+  |z|^p,&|z|>1,
+ \end{cases}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}|z|^p.
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The standard stable-kernel estimates recorded as properties (G)(ii)--(iii)
+by Ishige--Kawakami--Michihisa
+\cite{IshigeKawakamiMichihisa2017} give, with constants depending on the
+chosen stable scale,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}
+ c(1+|y|)^{-\beta}\le p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)
+ \le C(1+|y|)^{-\beta},\qquad
+ |\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)|
+ \le C_\eta(1+|y|)^{-\beta-|\eta|}.
+\end{equation}
+In particular every quotient
+\(\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}/p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) is bounded.  The upper
+bound in \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} follows from
+\[
+ \begin{aligned}
+ \int p_1(y-z)^q p_1(y)^{1-q}\dd y
+ &\le C\int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta q}
+              (1+|y|)^{\beta(q-1)}\dd y\\
+ &\le C(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+       \int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta}\dd y,
+ \end{aligned}
+\]
+where \(p_1=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) and
+\(1+|y|\le(1+|z|)(1+|y-z|)\).  The final integral is finite because
+\(\beta>d\).  For the lower bound, integrate over \(|y-z|\le1\) and use
+\eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}; this gives the claimed power
+for \(|z|\ge2\).  Positivity and continuity on bounded \(z\)-sets complete
+the estimate.
+
+For \(|z|\le1\), Taylor's formula and the bounded derivative quotients give
+the pointwise bound
+\(|F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)|\le C|z|^{m+1}\), uniformly
+in \(y\).  For \(|z|>1\), \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} gives
+\(\|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_q\le C|z|^{\beta(1-1/q)}\).  The Taylor
+coefficients are bounded, so
+\(\|T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_q\le C|z|^m\).  Finally,
+\[
+ \beta(1-1/q)\le p,\qquad m\le p<m+1,
+\]
+with equality in the first relation when \(\beta>4\).  These observations
+prove \eqref{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}.
+\end{proof}

+Write \(\Omega_{\alpha,d}(\dd y)=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)\dd y\) and
