+\begin{lemma}[Stable critical translation remainder]
+\label{lem:stable-critical-translation-remainder}
+Let \(d\ge1\), \(0<\alpha<2\), \(p=p_{\alpha,d}\),
+\(q=q_{\alpha,d}\), and \(m=\lfloor p\rfloor\).  If
+\(T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)\) is the Taylor polynomial of
+\(F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\) at \(z=0\) through degree \(m\), then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth}
+ c_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+ \le \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}^q
+ \le C_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}.
+\end{equation}
+Moreover,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}
+ \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}
+ \begin{cases}
+  |z|^{m+1},&|z|\le1,\\
+  |z|^p,&|z|>1,
+ \end{cases}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}|z|^p.
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The standard stable-kernel estimates recorded as properties (G)(ii)--(iii)
+by Ishige--Kawakami--Michihisa
+\cite{IshigeKawakamiMichihisa2017} give, with constants depending on the
+chosen stable scale,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}
+ c(1+|y|)^{-\beta}\le p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)
+ \le C(1+|y|)^{-\beta},\qquad
+ |\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)|
+ \le C_\eta(1+|y|)^{-\beta-|\eta|}.
+\end{equation}
+In particular every quotient
+\(\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}/p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) is bounded.  The upper
+bound in \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} follows from
+\[
+ \begin{aligned}
+ \int p_1(y-z)^q p_1(y)^{1-q}\dd y
+ &\le C\int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta q}
+              (1+|y|)^{\beta(q-1)}\dd y\\
+ &\le C(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+       \int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta}\dd y,
+ \end{aligned}
+\]
+where \(p_1=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) and
+\(1+|y|\le(1+|z|)(1+|y-z|)\).  The final integral is finite because
+\(\beta>d\).  For the lower bound, integrate over \(|y-z|\le1\) and use
+\eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}; this gives the claimed power
+for \(|z|\ge2\).  Positivity and continuity on bounded \(z\)-sets complete
+the estimate.
+
+For \(|z|\le1\), Taylor's formula and the bounded derivative quotients give
+the pointwise bound
+\(|F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)|\le C|z|^{m+1}\), uniformly
+in \(y\).  For \(|z|>1\), \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} gives
+\(\|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_q\le C|z|^{\beta(1-1/q)}\).  The Taylor
+coefficients are bounded, so
+\(\|T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_q\le C|z|^m\).  Finally,
+\[
+ \beta(1-1/q)\le p,\qquad m\le p<m+1,
+\]
+with equality in the first relation when \(\beta>4\).  These observations
+prove \eqref{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}.
+\end{proof}

+\begin{lemma}[Stable critical translation remainder]
+\label{lem:stable-critical-translation-remainder}
+Let \(d\ge1\), \(0<\alpha<2\), \(p=p_{\alpha,d}\),
+\(q=q_{\alpha,d}\), and \(m=\lfloor p\rfloor\).  If
+\(T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)\) is the Taylor polynomial of
+\(F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\) at \(z=0\) through degree \(m\), then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth}
+ c_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+ \le \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}^q
+ \le C_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}.
+\end{equation}
+Moreover,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}
+ \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}
+ \begin{cases}
+  |z|^{m+1},&|z|\le1,\\
+  |z|^p,&|z|>1,
+ \end{cases}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}|z|^p.
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The standard stable-kernel estimates recorded as properties (G)(ii)--(iii)
+by Ishige--Kawakami--Michihisa
+\cite{IshigeKawakamiMichihisa2017} give, with constants depending on the
+chosen stable scale,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}
+ c(1+|y|)^{-\beta}\le p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)
+ \le C(1+|y|)^{-\beta},\qquad
+ |\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)|
+ \le C_\eta(1+|y|)^{-\beta-|\eta|}.
+\end{equation}
+In particular every quotient
+\(\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}/p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) is bounded.  The upper
+bound in \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} follows from
+\[
+ \begin{aligned}
+ \int p_1(y-z)^q p_1(y)^{1-q}\dd y
+ &\le C\int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta q}
+              (1+|y|)^{\beta(q-1)}\dd y\\
+ &\le C(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+       \int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta}\dd y,
+ \end{aligned}
+\]
+where \(p_1=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) and
+\(1+|y|\le(1+|z|)(1+|y-z|)\).  The final integral is finite because
+\(\beta>d\).  For the lower bound, integrate over \(|y-z|\le1\) and use
+\eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}; this gives the claimed power
+for \(|z|\ge2\).  Positivity and continuity on bounded \(z\)-sets complete
+the estimate.
+
+For \(|z|\le1\), Taylor's formula and the bounded derivative quotients give
+the pointwise bound
+\(|F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)|\le C|z|^{m+1}\), uniformly
+in \(y\).  For \(|z|>1\), \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} gives
+\(\|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_q\le C|z|^{\beta(1-1/q)}\).  The Taylor
+coefficients are bounded, so
+\(\|T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_q\le C|z|^m\).  Finally,
+\[
+ \beta(1-1/q)\le p,\qquad m\le p<m+1,
+\]
+with equality in the first relation when \(\beta>4\).  These observations
+prove \eqref{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}.
+\end{proof}

# Literature Check: Regularly Varying Poisson-Entropy Boundary Layer

Checked 2026-08-02 (Asia/Singapore). The search target was the
coefficient-subtracted large-scale asymptotic

\[
t^{2N}\left\{
D_{\mathrm{KL}}(P_t*\nu\Vert P_t)
-\sum_{j=2}^{N-1}A_{2j}(\nu)t^{-2j}
\right\}
\]

for a fixed centred law whose tail is regularly varying with the exact
missing-moment index \(2N-2\).

## Standard External Inputs

The new proof invokes only the regular-variation results in the first item
below. The remaining items are exact contextual comparators; their theorems
are not imported into the boundary-layer proof.

- N. H. Bingham, C. M. Goldie, and J. L. Teugels,
  *Regular Variation*, Cambridge University Press, 1987,
  DOI 10.1017/CBO9780511721434. Proposition 1.5.9a supplies the divergent
  integrated-slow-variation fact
  \(L(t)=o(\int^tL(s)\,ds/s)\); Theorem 1.5.11 supplies Karamata's
  direct and tail integral theorems. This is the only external theorem used
  in the new proof.
- Laurens de Haan and Ana Ferreira, *Extreme Value Theory: An
  Introduction*, Springer, 2006, DOI 10.1007/0-387-34471-3. This records the
  de Haan/second-order regular-variation framework. No second-order theorem
  from this source is used; the paper explicitly leaves second-order entropy
  corrections open.
- N. G. de Bruijn, *A property of heat equation connected with Shannon's
  theory of information*, Nederl. Akad. Wetensch. Proc. Ser. A 56 (1953),
  80-81. No DOI or arXiv identifier was found. This is historical context,
  not a proof input.
- The Hardy--Stein and stable-entropy papers listed above are contextual
  comparators, not proof inputs.

DOI metadata for the books and journal articles was independently checked

## Novelty Determination

No arXiv record located by the targeted or comparator queries states the
following combination: a fixed centred input law, harmonic Poisson/Cauchy
smoothing, subtraction of all finite Cayley--entropy coefficients below the
missing moment, a tail index exactly \(2N-2\), and the explicit limit
normalized by
\(\ell_L(t)=\int^tL(s)\,ds/s\).

The nearest results separate into three established bodies of work:
Karamata/de Haan regular-variation theory; de Bruijn or Hardy--Stein entropy
dissipation identities; and entropic convergence to stable laws. The
manuscript cites those inputs and does not claim any of their theorems as
new. Its new statement is the quotient-to-entropy synthesis yielding the
constant
\[
p(c_++c_-)(-1)^N(N-1)2^{-2N+2}\mu_2.
\]

This is a documented negative literature search, not a logically exhaustive
proof that no publication exists outside the indexed sources. Within the
queried arXiv corpus and the standard references/comparators above, no prior
publication of the stated theorem was found.

exact large-scale decomposition of radial Poisson relative entropy into the
quadratic covariance coefficient and the relative entropy from a

A Crossref bibliographic search for `Poisson kernel relative entropy
covariance deficit` returned Poisson-channel and Poisson-approximation papers,

the covariance-proxy decomposition.  The closest standard information-theory
inputs remain the classical data-processing and finite-partition
characterizations of relative entropy; those facts are not claimed as new.

No indexed source located in this search gives the combination of a fixed
input law with only finite covariance, harmonic Poisson smoothing, the
explicit bounded mode (b_\Sigma), and the asymptotic identity

\[

\]

As above, this is a documented negative search rather than a logically
exhaustive proof of absence from all literature.

+Write \(\Omega_{\alpha,d}(\dd y)=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)\dd y\) and

+\begin{lemma}[Stable critical translation remainder]
+\label{lem:stable-critical-translation-remainder}
+Let \(d\ge1\), \(0<\alpha<2\), \(p=p_{\alpha,d}\),
+\(q=q_{\alpha,d}\), and \(m=\lfloor p\rfloor\).  If
+\(T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)\) is the Taylor polynomial of
+\(F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\) at \(z=0\) through degree \(m\), then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth}
+ c_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+ \le \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}^q
+ \le C_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}.
+\end{equation}
+Moreover,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}
+ \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}
+ \begin{cases}
+  |z|^{m+1},&|z|\le1,\\
+  |z|^p,&|z|>1,
+ \end{cases}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}|z|^p.
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The standard stable-kernel estimates recorded as properties (G)(ii)--(iii)
+by Ishige--Kawakami--Michihisa
+\cite{IshigeKawakamiMichihisa2017} give, with constants depending on the
+chosen stable scale,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}
+ c(1+|y|)^{-\beta}\le p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)
+ \le C(1+|y|)^{-\beta},\qquad
+ |\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)|
+ \le C_\eta(1+|y|)^{-\beta-|\eta|}.
+\end{equation}
+In particular every quotient
+\(\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}/p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) is bounded.  The upper
+bound in \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} follows from
+\[
+ \begin{aligned}
+ \int p_1(y-z)^q p_1(y)^{1-q}\dd y
+ &\le C\int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta q}
+              (1+|y|)^{\beta(q-1)}\dd y\\
+ &\le C(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+       \int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta}\dd y,
+ \end{aligned}
+\]
+where \(p_1=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) and
+\(1+|y|\le(1+|z|)(1+|y-z|)\).  The final integral is finite because
+\(\beta>d\).  For the lower bound, integrate over \(|y-z|\le1\) and use
+\eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}; this gives the claimed power
+for \(|z|\ge2\).  Positivity and continuity on bounded \(z\)-sets complete
+the estimate.
+
+For \(|z|\le1\), Taylor's formula and the bounded derivative quotients give
+the pointwise bound
+\(|F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)|\le C|z|^{m+1}\), uniformly
+in \(y\).  For \(|z|>1\), \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} gives
+\(\|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_q\le C|z|^{\beta(1-1/q)}\).  The Taylor
+coefficients are bounded, so
+\(\|T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_q\le C|z|^m\).  Finally,
+\[
+ \beta(1-1/q)\le p,\qquad m\le p<m+1,
+\]
+with equality in the first relation when \(\beta>4\).  These observations
+prove \eqref{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}.
+\end{proof}

+\eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds} and \(s_j/R_j\to0\) give
+\[
+ p_{s_j}^{(\alpha,d)}(A_j)
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}(s_j/R_j)^\beta
+ =C_{\alpha,d}\kappa^\beta w_j.
+\]
+Choose \(\kappa\) so that the second Bernoulli mass is a fixed small
+fraction of the first.  Data processing to
+\(\{A_j,A_j^c\}\) then yields \(H_{\alpha,d}(s_j)\ge c w_j\), and hence
 \[
- t_j^4H_d(t_j)\ge c_dR_j^4w_j^{1+4/(d+1)}
- =c_d\alpha_j^{q_d}R_j^{4-rq_d}.
+ s_j^4H_{\alpha,d}(s_j)
+ \ge cR_j^4w_j^{1+4/\beta}
+ =ca_j^{q_{\alpha,d}}R_j^{4-rq_{\alpha,d}}.
 \]
-Since \(r<p_d=4/q_d\), the exponent of \(R_j\) is positive.  Recursive
-choice of the radii makes this expression unbounded while preserving the
-finite \(r\)th moment and, after adding a bounded spanning component, a
-positive-definite covariance.
+Here \(q_{\alpha,d}=1+4/\beta\) and
+\(r<p=4/q_{\alpha,d}\), so the exponent of \(R_j\) is positive.
+Recursive choice of the radii makes \(s_j\to\infty\) and the last display
+unbounded while preserving all moment assertions.
 \end{proof}

 As above, this is a documented negative search rather than a logically
 exhaustive proof of absence from all literature.
+
+## Stable-Kernel Critical-Moment Search
+
+Checked 2026-08-08 (Asia/Singapore).  The search target was the optimal
+absolute-moment hypothesis for the covariance-order relative-entropy
+asymptotic of a fixed law smoothed by an isotropic strictly alpha-stable
+kernel, with the stable kernel itself as the translated reference.
+
+The nearest paper was inspected in full:
+
+- K. Ishige, T. Kawakami, and H. Michihisa, *Asymptotic Expansions of
+  Solutions of Fractional Diffusion Equations*, SIAM J. Math. Anal. 49
+  (2017), 2167--2190, arXiv:1610.09789,
+  DOI 10.1137/16M1101428.
+- K. Ishige and T. Kawakami, *Refined Asymptotic Expansions of Solutions to
+  Fractional Diffusion Equations*, J. Dynam. Differential Equations 36
+  (2024), 2679--2702, arXiv:2109.14193,
+  DOI 10.1007/s10884-022-10224-4.
+
+Their theorems, bibliographies, and forward-citation records were checked,
+along with Crossref, Semantic Scholar, zbMATH, and targeted arXiv searches
+for combinations of stable/fractional heat kernels, translated density
+quotients, relative entropy, asymptotic expansions, and moment conditions.
+The arXiv API returned HTTP 429 during this audit, so arXiv abstract pages,
+HTML, and PDFs were used to inspect the relevant records.  Google Scholar
+was also queried but returned its unusual-traffic interstitial; no Scholar
+results are therefore represented as inspected.
+
+Ishige--Kawakami--Michihisa prove density-level fractional-heat expansions:
+moment-weighted kernel derivatives are subtracted and the remainder is
+controlled in scaled L^q and weighted L^1 norms.  The refined paper extends
+that framework to inhomogeneous and nonlinear equations.  Neither paper
+states the critical matched-quotient estimate
+
+\[
+\left\|\frac{p_1(\mathord\cdot-z)}{p_1}\right\|_{L^q(p_1)}^q
+\asymp (1+|z|)^{(d+\alpha)(q-1)},
+\]
+
+uses it to transfer a moment expansion through relative entropy, or gives
+the uniform sufficient exponent
+
+\[
+p_{\alpha,d}=\max\left\{2,
+\frac{4(d+\alpha)}{d+\alpha+4}\right\}.
+\]
+
+The stable-entropy papers of Bobkov--Chistyakov--Goetze, Johnson, and
+Toscani concern convergence of normalized convolution sequences or entropy
+relative to a fixed stable target.  They do not address this fixed-input,
+large-spatial-scale, moving matched-reference problem.  No indexed source
+located in the audit states the exponent or the matching uniform
+moment-class optimality result.  This remains a qualified negative search,
+not a proof of absence from every publication.

+\label{lem:stable-critical-translation-remainder}
+Let \(d\ge1\), \(0<\alpha<2\), \(p=p_{\alpha,d}\),
+\(q=q_{\alpha,d}\), and \(m=\lfloor p\rfloor\).  If
+\(T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)\) is the Taylor polynomial of
+\(F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\) at \(z=0\) through degree \(m\), then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth}
+ c_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+ \le \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}^q
+ \le C_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}.
+\end{equation}
+Moreover,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}
+ \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}
+ \begin{cases}
+  |z|^{m+1},&|z|\le1,\\
+  |z|^p,&|z|>1,
+ \end{cases}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}|z|^p.
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The standard stable-kernel estimates recorded as properties (G)(ii)--(iii)
+by Ishige--Kawakami--Michihisa
+\cite{IshigeKawakamiMichihisa2017} give, with constants depending on the
+chosen stable scale,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}
+ c(1+|y|)^{-\beta}\le p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)
+ \le C(1+|y|)^{-\beta},\qquad
+ |\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)|
+ \le C_\eta(1+|y|)^{-\beta-|\eta|}.
+\end{equation}
+In particular every quotient
+\(\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}/p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) is bounded.  The upper
+bound in \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} follows from
+\[
+ \begin{aligned}
+ \int p_1(y-z)^q p_1(y)^{1-q}\dd y
+ &\le C\int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta q}
+              (1+|y|)^{\beta(q-1)}\dd y\\
+ &\le C(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+       \int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta}\dd y,
+ \end{aligned}
+\]
+where \(p_1=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) and
+\(1+|y|\le(1+|z|)(1+|y-z|)\).  The final integral is finite because
+\(\beta>d\).  For the lower bound, integrate over \(|y-z|\le1\) and use
+\eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}; this gives the claimed power
+for \(|z|\ge2\).  Positivity and continuity on bounded \(z\)-sets complete
+the estimate.
+
+For \(|z|\le1\), \eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds} also gives
+\(p_1(y-\theta z)\le C p_1(y)\), uniformly in \(0\le\theta\le1\).
+Taylor's formula along the segment from \(y\) to \(y-z\), followed by the
+derivative bound in \eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}, therefore
+gives the pointwise bound
+\(|F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)|\le C|z|^{m+1}\), uniformly
+in \(y\).  For \(|z|>1\), \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} gives
+\(\|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_q\le C|z|^{\beta(1-1/q)}\).  The Taylor
+coefficients are bounded, so
+\(\|T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_q\le C|z|^m\).  Finally,
+\[
+ \beta(1-1/q)\le p,\qquad m\le p<m+1,
+\]
+with equality in the first relation when \(\beta>4\).  These observations
+prove \eqref{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}.
+\end{proof}
+

 As above, this is a documented negative search rather than a logically
 exhaustive proof of absence from all literature.
+
+## Stable-Kernel Critical-Moment Search
+
+Checked 2026-08-08 (Asia/Singapore).  The search target was the optimal
+absolute-moment hypothesis for the covariance-order relative-entropy
+asymptotic of a fixed law smoothed by an isotropic strictly alpha-stable
+kernel, with the stable kernel itself as the translated reference.
+
+The nearest paper was inspected in full:
+
+- K. Ishige, T. Kawakami, and H. Michihisa, *Asymptotic Expansions of
+  Solutions of Fractional Diffusion Equations*, SIAM J. Math. Anal. 49
+  (2017), 2167--2190, arXiv:1610.09789,
+  DOI 10.1137/16M1101428.
+- K. Ishige and T. Kawakami, *Refined Asymptotic Expansions of Solutions to
+  Fractional Diffusion Equations*, J. Dynam. Differential Equations 36
+  (2024), 2679--2702, arXiv:2109.14193,
+  DOI 10.1007/s10884-022-10224-4.
+
+Their theorems, bibliographies, and forward-citation records were checked,
+along with Crossref, Semantic Scholar, zbMATH, and targeted arXiv searches
+for combinations of stable/fractional heat kernels, translated density
+quotients, relative entropy, asymptotic expansions, and moment conditions.
+The arXiv API returned HTTP 429 during this audit, so arXiv abstract pages,
+HTML, and PDFs were used to inspect the relevant records.  Google Scholar
+was also queried but returned its unusual-traffic interstitial; no Scholar
+results are therefore represented as inspected.
+
+Ishige--Kawakami--Michihisa prove density-level fractional-heat expansions:
+moment-weighted kernel derivatives are subtracted and the remainder is
+controlled in scaled L^q and weighted L^1 norms.  The refined paper extends
+that framework to inhomogeneous and nonlinear equations.  Neither paper
+states the critical matched-quotient estimate
+
+\[
+\left\|\frac{p_1(\mathord\cdot-z)}{p_1}\right\|_{L^q(p_1)}^q
+\asymp (1+|z|)^{(d+\alpha)(q-1)},
+\]
+
+uses it to transfer a moment expansion through relative entropy, or gives
+the uniform sufficient exponent
+
+\[
+p_{\alpha,d}=\max\left\{2,
+\frac{4(d+\alpha)}{d+\alpha+4}\right\}.
+\]
+
+The stable-entropy papers of Bobkov--Chistyakov--Goetze, Johnson, and
+Toscani concern convergence of normalized convolution sequences or entropy
+relative to a fixed stable target.  They do not address this fixed-input,
+large-spatial-scale, moving matched-reference problem.  No indexed source
+located in the audit states the exponent or the matching uniform
+moment-class optimality result.  This remains a qualified negative search,
+not a proof of absence from every publication.

+\begin{lemma}[Stable critical translation remainder]
+\label{lem:stable-critical-translation-remainder}
+Let \(d\ge1\), \(0<\alpha<2\), \(p=p_{\alpha,d}\),
+\(q=q_{\alpha,d}\), and \(m=\lfloor p\rfloor\).  If
+\(T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)\) is the Taylor polynomial of
+\(F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\) at \(z=0\) through degree \(m\), then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth}
+ c_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+ \le \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}^q
+ \le C_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}.
+\end{equation}
+Moreover,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}
+ \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}
+ \begin{cases}
+  |z|^{m+1},&|z|\le1,\\
+  |z|^p,&|z|>1,
+ \end{cases}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}|z|^p.
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The standard stable-kernel estimates recorded as properties (G)(ii)--(iii)
+by Ishige--Kawakami--Michihisa
+\cite{IshigeKawakamiMichihisa2017} give, with constants depending on the
+chosen stable scale,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}
+ c(1+|y|)^{-\beta}\le p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)
+ \le C(1+|y|)^{-\beta},\qquad
+ |\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)|
+ \le C_\eta(1+|y|)^{-\beta-|\eta|}.
+\end{equation}
+In particular every quotient
+\(\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}/p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) is bounded.  The upper
+bound in \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} follows from
+\[
+ \begin{aligned}
+ \int p_1(y-z)^q p_1(y)^{1-q}\dd y
+ &\le C\int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta q}
+              (1+|y|)^{\beta(q-1)}\dd y\\
+ &\le C(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+       \int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta}\dd y,
+ \end{aligned}
+\]
+where \(p_1=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) and
+\(1+|y|\le(1+|z|)(1+|y-z|)\).  The final integral is finite because
+\(\beta>d\).  For the lower bound, integrate over \(|y-z|\le1\) and use
+\eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}; this gives the claimed power
+for \(|z|\ge2\).  Positivity and continuity on bounded \(z\)-sets complete
+the estimate.
+
+For \(|z|\le1\), \eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds} also gives
+\(p_1(y-\theta z)\le C p_1(y)\), uniformly in \(0\le\theta\le1\).
+Taylor's formula along the segment from \(y\) to \(y-z\), followed by the
+derivative bound in \eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}, therefore
+gives the pointwise bound
+\(|F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)|\le C|z|^{m+1}\), uniformly
+in \(y\).  For \(|z|>1\), \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} gives
+\(\|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_q\le C|z|^{\beta(1-1/q)}\).  The Taylor
+coefficients are bounded, so
+\(\|T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_q\le C|z|^m\).  Finally,
+\[
+ \beta(1-1/q)\le p,\qquad m\le p<m+1,
+\]
+with equality in the first relation when \(\beta>4\).  These observations
+prove \eqref{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}.
+\end{proof}

 As above, this is a documented negative search rather than a logically
 exhaustive proof of absence from all literature.
+
+## Stable-Kernel Critical-Moment Search
+
+Checked 2026-08-08 (Asia/Singapore).  The search target was the optimal
+absolute-moment hypothesis for the covariance-order relative-entropy
+asymptotic of a fixed law smoothed by an isotropic strictly alpha-stable
+kernel, with the stable kernel itself as the translated reference.
+
+The nearest paper was inspected in full:
+
+- K. Ishige, T. Kawakami, and H. Michihisa, *Asymptotic Expansions of
+  Solutions of Fractional Diffusion Equations*, SIAM J. Math. Anal. 49
+  (2017), 2167--2190, arXiv:1610.09789,
+  DOI 10.1137/16M1101428.
+- K. Ishige and T. Kawakami, *Refined Asymptotic Expansions of Solutions to
+  Fractional Diffusion Equations*, J. Dynam. Differential Equations 36
+  (2024), 2679--2702, arXiv:2109.14193,
+  DOI 10.1007/s10884-022-10224-4.
+
+Their theorems, bibliographies, and forward-citation records were checked,
+along with Crossref, Semantic Scholar, zbMATH, and targeted arXiv searches
+for combinations of stable/fractional heat kernels, translated density
+quotients, relative entropy, asymptotic expansions, and moment conditions.
+The arXiv API returned HTTP 429 during this audit, so arXiv abstract pages,
+HTML, and PDFs were used to inspect the relevant records.  Google Scholar
+was also queried but returned its unusual-traffic interstitial; no Scholar
+results are therefore represented as inspected.
+
+Ishige--Kawakami--Michihisa prove density-level fractional-heat expansions:
+moment-weighted kernel derivatives are subtracted and the remainder is
+controlled in scaled L^q and weighted L^1 norms.  The refined paper extends
+that framework to inhomogeneous and nonlinear equations.  Neither paper
+states the critical matched-quotient estimate
+
+\[
+\left\|\frac{p_1(\mathord\cdot-z)}{p_1}\right\|_{L^q(p_1)}^q
+\asymp (1+|z|)^{(d+\alpha)(q-1)},
+\]
+
+uses it to transfer a moment expansion through relative entropy, or gives
+the uniform sufficient exponent
+
+\[
+p_{\alpha,d}=\max\left\{2,
+\frac{4(d+\alpha)}{d+\alpha+4}\right\}.
+\]
+
+The stable-entropy papers of Bobkov--Chistyakov--Goetze, Johnson, and
+Toscani concern convergence of normalized convolution sequences or entropy
+relative to a fixed stable target.  They do not address this fixed-input,
+large-spatial-scale, moving matched-reference problem.  No indexed source
+located in the audit states the exponent or the matching uniform
+moment-class optimality result.  This remains a qualified negative search,
+not a proof of absence from every publication.

+Write \(\Omega_{\alpha,d}(\dd y)=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)\dd y\) and

+\begin{lemma}[Stable critical translation remainder]
+\label{lem:stable-critical-translation-remainder}
+Let \(d\ge1\), \(0<\alpha<2\), \(p=p_{\alpha,d}\),
+\(q=q_{\alpha,d}\), and \(m=\lfloor p\rfloor\).  If
+\(T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)\) is the Taylor polynomial of
+\(F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\) at \(z=0\) through degree \(m\), then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth}
+ c_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+ \le \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}^q
+ \le C_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}.
+\end{equation}
+Moreover,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}
+ \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}
+ \begin{cases}
+  |z|^{m+1},&|z|\le1,\\
+  |z|^p,&|z|>1,
+ \end{cases}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}|z|^p.
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The standard stable-kernel estimates recorded as properties (G)(ii)--(iii)
+by Ishige--Kawakami--Michihisa
+\cite{IshigeKawakamiMichihisa2017} give, with constants depending on the
+chosen stable scale,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}
+ c(1+|y|)^{-\beta}\le p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)
+ \le C(1+|y|)^{-\beta},\qquad
+ |\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)|
+ \le C_\eta(1+|y|)^{-\beta-|\eta|}.
+\end{equation}
+In particular every quotient
+\(\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}/p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) is bounded.  The upper
+bound in \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} follows from
+\[
+ \begin{aligned}
+ \int p_1(y-z)^q p_1(y)^{1-q}\dd y
+ &\le C\int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta q}
+              (1+|y|)^{\beta(q-1)}\dd y\\
+ &\le C(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+       \int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta}\dd y,
+ \end{aligned}
+\]
+where \(p_1=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) and
+\(1+|y|\le(1+|z|)(1+|y-z|)\).  The final integral is finite because
+\(\beta>d\).  For the lower bound, integrate over \(|y-z|\le1\) and use
+\eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}; this gives the claimed power
+for \(|z|\ge2\).  Positivity and continuity on bounded \(z\)-sets complete
+the estimate.
+
+For \(|z|\le1\), \eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds} also gives
+\(p_1(y-\theta z)\le C p_1(y)\), uniformly in \(0\le\theta\le1\).
+Taylor's formula along the segment from \(y\) to \(y-z\), followed by the
+derivative bound in \eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}, therefore
+gives the pointwise bound
+\(|F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)|\le C|z|^{m+1}\), uniformly
+in \(y\).  For \(|z|>1\), \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} gives
+\(\|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_q\le C|z|^{\beta(1-1/q)}\).  The Taylor
+coefficients are bounded, so
+\(\|T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_q\le C|z|^m\).  Finally,
+\[
+ \beta(1-1/q)\le p,\qquad m\le p<m+1,
+\]
+with equality in the first relation when \(\beta>4\).  These observations
+prove \eqref{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}.
+\end{proof}

 As above, this is a documented negative search rather than a logically
 exhaustive proof of absence from all literature.
+
+## Stable-Kernel Critical-Moment Search
+
+Checked 2026-08-08 (Asia/Singapore).  The search target was the optimal
+absolute-moment hypothesis for the covariance-order relative-entropy
+asymptotic of a fixed law smoothed by an isotropic strictly alpha-stable
+kernel, with the stable kernel itself as the translated reference.
+
+The nearest paper was inspected in full:
+
+- K. Ishige, T. Kawakami, and H. Michihisa, *Asymptotic Expansions of
+  Solutions of Fractional Diffusion Equations*, SIAM J. Math. Anal. 49
+  (2017), 2167--2190, arXiv:1610.09789,
+  DOI 10.1137/16M1101428.
+- K. Ishige and T. Kawakami, *Refined Asymptotic Expansions of Solutions to
+  Fractional Diffusion Equations*, J. Dynam. Differential Equations 36
+  (2024), 2679--2702, arXiv:2109.14193,
+  DOI 10.1007/s10884-022-10224-4.
+
+Their theorems, bibliographies, and forward-citation records were checked,
+along with Crossref, Semantic Scholar, zbMATH, and targeted arXiv searches
+for combinations of stable/fractional heat kernels, translated density
+quotients, relative entropy, asymptotic expansions, and moment conditions.
+The arXiv API returned HTTP 429 during this audit, so arXiv abstract pages,
+HTML, and PDFs were used to inspect the relevant records.  Google Scholar
+was also queried but returned its unusual-traffic interstitial; no Scholar
+results are therefore represented as inspected.
+
+Ishige--Kawakami--Michihisa prove density-level fractional-heat expansions:
+moment-weighted kernel derivatives are subtracted and the remainder is
+controlled in scaled L^q and weighted L^1 norms.  The refined paper extends
+that framework to inhomogeneous and nonlinear equations.  Neither paper
+states the critical matched-quotient estimate
+
+\[
+\left\|\frac{p_1(\mathord\cdot-z)}{p_1}\right\|_{L^q(p_1)}^q
+\asymp (1+|z|)^{(d+\alpha)(q-1)},
+\]
+
+uses it to transfer a moment expansion through relative entropy, or gives
+the uniform sufficient exponent
+
+\[
+p_{\alpha,d}=\max\left\{2,
+\frac{4(d+\alpha)}{d+\alpha+4}\right\}.
+\]
+
+The stable-entropy papers of Bobkov--Chistyakov--Goetze, Johnson, and
+Toscani concern convergence of normalized convolution sequences or entropy
+relative to a fixed stable target.  They do not address this fixed-input,
+large-spatial-scale, moving matched-reference problem.  No indexed source
+located in the audit states the exponent or the matching uniform
+moment-class optimality result.  This remains a qualified negative search,
+not a proof of absence from every publication.

+\begin{lemma}[Stable critical translation remainder]
+\label{lem:stable-critical-translation-remainder}
+Let \(d\ge1\), \(0<\alpha<2\), \(p=p_{\alpha,d}\),
+\(q=q_{\alpha,d}\), and \(m=\lfloor p\rfloor\).  If
+\(T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)\) is the Taylor polynomial of
+\(F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\) at \(z=0\) through degree \(m\), then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth}
+ c_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+ \le \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}^q
+ \le C_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}.
+\end{equation}
+Moreover,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}
+ \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}
+ \begin{cases}
+  |z|^{m+1},&|z|\le1,\\
+  |z|^p,&|z|>1,
+ \end{cases}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}|z|^p.
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The standard stable-kernel estimates recorded as properties (G)(ii)--(iii)
+by Ishige--Kawakami--Michihisa
+\cite{IshigeKawakamiMichihisa2017} give, with constants depending on the
+chosen stable scale,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}
+ c(1+|y|)^{-\beta}\le p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)
+ \le C(1+|y|)^{-\beta},\qquad
+ |\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)|
+ \le C_\eta(1+|y|)^{-\beta-|\eta|}.
+\end{equation}
+In particular every quotient
+\(\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}/p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) is bounded.  The upper
+bound in \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} follows from
+\[
+ \begin{aligned}
+ \int p_1(y-z)^q p_1(y)^{1-q}\dd y
+ &\le C\int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta q}
+              (1+|y|)^{\beta(q-1)}\dd y\\
+ &\le C(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+       \int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta}\dd y,
+ \end{aligned}
+\]
+where \(p_1=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) and
+\(1+|y|\le(1+|z|)(1+|y-z|)\).  The final integral is finite because
+\(\beta>d\).  For the lower bound, integrate over \(|y-z|\le1\) and use
+\eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}; this gives the claimed power
+for \(|z|\ge2\).  Positivity and continuity on bounded \(z\)-sets complete
+the estimate.
+
+For \(|z|\le1\), \eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds} also gives
+\(p_1(y-\theta z)\le C p_1(y)\), uniformly in \(0\le\theta\le1\).
+Taylor's formula along the segment from \(y\) to \(y-z\), followed by the
+derivative bound in \eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}, therefore
+gives the pointwise bound
+\(|F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)|\le C|z|^{m+1}\), uniformly
+in \(y\).  For \(|z|>1\), \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} gives
+\(\|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_q\le C|z|^{\beta(1-1/q)}\).  The Taylor
+coefficients are bounded, so
+\(\|T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_q\le C|z|^m\).  Finally,
+\[
+ \beta(1-1/q)\le p,\qquad m\le p<m+1,
+\]
+with equality in the first relation when \(\beta>4\).  These observations
+prove \eqref{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}.
+\end{proof}

 As above, this is a documented negative search rather than a logically
 exhaustive proof of absence from all literature.
+
+## Stable-Kernel Critical-Moment Search
+
+Checked 2026-08-08 (Asia/Singapore).  The search target was the optimal
+absolute-moment hypothesis for the covariance-order relative-entropy
+asymptotic of a fixed law smoothed by an isotropic strictly alpha-stable
+kernel, with the stable kernel itself as the translated reference.
+
+The nearest paper was inspected in full:
+
+- K. Ishige, T. Kawakami, and H. Michihisa, *Asymptotic Expansions of
+  Solutions of Fractional Diffusion Equations*, SIAM J. Math. Anal. 49
+  (2017), 2167--2190, arXiv:1610.09789,
+  DOI 10.1137/16M1101428.
+- K. Ishige and T. Kawakami, *Refined Asymptotic Expansions of Solutions to
+  Fractional Diffusion Equations*, J. Dynam. Differential Equations 36
+  (2024), 2679--2702, arXiv:2109.14193,
+  DOI 10.1007/s10884-022-10224-4.
+
+Their theorems, bibliographies, and forward-citation records were checked,
+along with Crossref, Semantic Scholar, zbMATH, and targeted arXiv searches
+for combinations of stable/fractional heat kernels, translated density
+quotients, relative entropy, asymptotic expansions, and moment conditions.
+The arXiv API returned HTTP 429 during this audit, so arXiv abstract pages,
+HTML, and PDFs were used to inspect the relevant records.  Google Scholar
+was also queried but returned its unusual-traffic interstitial; no Scholar
+results are therefore represented as inspected.
+
+Ishige--Kawakami--Michihisa prove density-level fractional-heat expansions:
+moment-weighted kernel derivatives are subtracted and the remainder is
+controlled in scaled L^q and weighted L^1 norms.  The refined paper extends
+that framework to inhomogeneous and nonlinear equations.  Neither paper
+states the critical matched-quotient estimate
+
+\[
+\left\|\frac{p_1(\mathord\cdot-z)}{p_1}\right\|_{L^q(p_1)}^q
+\asymp (1+|z|)^{(d+\alpha)(q-1)},
+\]
+
+uses it to transfer a moment expansion through relative entropy, or gives
+the uniform sufficient exponent
+
+\[
+p_{\alpha,d}=\max\left\{2,
+\frac{4(d+\alpha)}{d+\alpha+4}\right\}.
+\]
+
+The stable-entropy papers of Bobkov--Chistyakov--Goetze, Johnson, and
+Toscani concern convergence of normalized convolution sequences or entropy
+relative to a fixed stable target.  They do not address this fixed-input,
+large-spatial-scale, moving matched-reference problem.  No indexed source
+located in the audit states the exponent or the matching uniform
+moment-class optimality result.  This remains a qualified negative search,
+not a proof of absence from every publication.

+centred isotropic strictly \(\alpha\)-stable law on \(\RR^d\), and use the
+spatial-scale normalization
+\[
+ p_s^{(\alpha,d)}(x)=s^{-d}p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(x/s),\qquad s>0.

+Changing the scale parameter in the characteristic exponent only changes
+the choice of \(p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\), so this notation covers every isotropic
+strictly stable kernel.  Put
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-critical-exponents}
+ \beta=d+\alpha,\qquad
+ q_{\alpha,d}:=\min\left\{2,1+\frac4\beta\right\},\qquad
+ p_{\alpha,d}:=\frac4{q_{\alpha,d}}
+ =\max\left\{2,\frac{4(d+\alpha)}{d+\alpha+4}\right\}.
+\end{equation}
+Write \(\Omega_{\alpha,d}(\dd y)=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)\dd y\) and
+\[
+ F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)
+ :=\frac{p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y-z)}{p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)}.

+\begin{lemma}[Stable critical translation remainder]
+\label{lem:stable-critical-translation-remainder}
+Let \(d\ge1\), \(0<\alpha<2\), \(p=p_{\alpha,d}\),
+\(q=q_{\alpha,d}\), and \(m=\lfloor p\rfloor\).  If
+\(T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)\) is the Taylor polynomial of
+\(F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\) at \(z=0\) through degree \(m\), then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth}
+ c_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+ \le \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}^q
+ \le C_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}.
+\end{equation}
+Moreover,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}
+ \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}
+ \begin{cases}
+  |z|^{m+1},&|z|\le1,\\
+  |z|^p,&|z|>1,
+ \end{cases}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}|z|^p.
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The standard stable-kernel estimates recorded as properties (G)(ii)--(iii)
+by Ishige--Kawakami--Michihisa
+\cite{IshigeKawakamiMichihisa2017} give, with constants depending on the
+chosen stable scale,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}
+ c(1+|y|)^{-\beta}\le p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)
+ \le C(1+|y|)^{-\beta},\qquad
+ |\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)|
+ \le C_\eta(1+|y|)^{-\beta-|\eta|}.
+\end{equation}
+In particular every quotient
+\(\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}/p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) is bounded.  The upper
+bound in \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} follows from
+\[
+ \begin{aligned}
+ \int p_1(y-z)^q p_1(y)^{1-q}\dd y
+ &\le C\int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta q}
+              (1+|y|)^{\beta(q-1)}\dd y\\
+ &\le C(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+       \int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta}\dd y,
+ \end{aligned}
+\]
+where \(p_1=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) and
+\(1+|y|\le(1+|z|)(1+|y-z|)\).  The final integral is finite because
+\(\beta>d\).  For the lower bound, integrate over \(|y-z|\le1\) and use
+\eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}; this gives the claimed power
+for \(|z|\ge2\).  Positivity and continuity on bounded \(z\)-sets complete
+the estimate.
+
+For \(|z|\le1\), \eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds} also gives
+\(p_1(y-\theta z)\le C p_1(y)\), uniformly in \(0\le\theta\le1\).
+Taylor's formula along the segment from \(y\) to \(y-z\), followed by the
+derivative bound in \eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}, therefore
+gives the pointwise bound
+\(|F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)|\le C|z|^{m+1}\), uniformly
+in \(y\).  For \(|z|>1\), \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} gives
+\(\|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_q\le C|z|^{\beta(1-1/q)}\).  The Taylor
+coefficients are bounded, so
+\(\|T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_q\le C|z|^m\).  Finally,
+\[
+ \beta(1-1/q)\le p,\qquad m\le p<m+1,
+\]
+with equality in the first relation when \(\beta>4\).  These observations
+prove \eqref{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}.
+\end{proof}

+Here \(q_{\alpha,d}=1+4/\beta\) and
+\(r<p=4/q_{\alpha,d}\), so the exponent of \(R_j\) is positive.
+Recursive choice of the radii makes \(s_j\to\infty\) and the last display
+unbounded while preserving all moment assertions.
 \end{proof}

 As above, this is a documented negative search rather than a logically
 exhaustive proof of absence from all literature.
+
+## Stable-Kernel Critical-Moment Search
+
+Checked 2026-08-08 (Asia/Singapore).  The search target was the optimal
+absolute-moment hypothesis for the covariance-order relative-entropy
+asymptotic of a fixed law smoothed by an isotropic strictly alpha-stable
+kernel, with the stable kernel itself as the translated reference.
+
+The nearest paper was inspected in full:
+
+- K. Ishige, T. Kawakami, and H. Michihisa, *Asymptotic Expansions of
+  Solutions of Fractional Diffusion Equations*, SIAM J. Math. Anal. 49
+  (2017), 2167--2190, arXiv:1610.09789,
+  DOI 10.1137/16M1101428.
+- K. Ishige and T. Kawakami, *Refined Asymptotic Expansions of Solutions to
+  Fractional Diffusion Equations*, J. Dynam. Differential Equations 36
+  (2024), 2679--2702, arXiv:2109.14193,
+  DOI 10.1007/s10884-022-10224-4.
+
+Their theorems, bibliographies, and forward-citation records were checked,
+along with Crossref, Semantic Scholar, zbMATH, and targeted arXiv searches
+for combinations of stable/fractional heat kernels, translated density
+quotients, relative entropy, asymptotic expansions, and moment conditions.
+The arXiv API returned HTTP 429 during this audit, so arXiv abstract pages,
+HTML, and PDFs were used to inspect the relevant records.  Google Scholar
+was also queried but returned its unusual-traffic interstitial; no Scholar
+results are therefore represented as inspected.
+
+Ishige--Kawakami--Michihisa prove density-level fractional-heat expansions:
+moment-weighted kernel derivatives are subtracted and the remainder is
+controlled in scaled L^q and weighted L^1 norms.  The refined paper extends
+that framework to inhomogeneous and nonlinear equations.  Neither paper
+states the critical matched-quotient estimate
+
+\[
+\left\|\frac{p_1(\mathord\cdot-z)}{p_1}\right\|_{L^q(p_1)}^q
+\asymp (1+|z|)^{(d+\alpha)(q-1)},
+\]
+
+uses it to transfer a moment expansion through relative entropy, or gives
+the uniform sufficient exponent
+
+\[
+p_{\alpha,d}=\max\left\{2,
+\frac{4(d+\alpha)}{d+\alpha+4}\right\}.
+\]
+
+The stable-entropy papers of Bobkov--Chistyakov--Goetze, Johnson, and
+Toscani concern convergence of normalized convolution sequences or entropy
+relative to a fixed stable target.  They do not address this fixed-input,
+large-spatial-scale, moving matched-reference problem.  No indexed source
+located in the audit states the exponent or the matching uniform
+moment-class optimality result.  This remains a qualified negative search,
+not a proof of absence from every publication.

+ \beta=d+\alpha,\qquad

+\begin{lemma}[Stable critical translation remainder]
+\label{lem:stable-critical-translation-remainder}
+Let \(d\ge1\), \(0<\alpha<2\), \(p=p_{\alpha,d}\),
+\(q=q_{\alpha,d}\), and \(m=\lfloor p\rfloor\).  If
+\(T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)\) is the Taylor polynomial of
+\(F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\) at \(z=0\) through degree \(m\), then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth}
+ c_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+ \le \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}^q
+ \le C_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}.
+\end{equation}
+Moreover,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}
+ \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}
+ \begin{cases}
+  |z|^{m+1},&|z|\le1,\\
+  |z|^p,&|z|>1,
+ \end{cases}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}|z|^p.
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The standard stable-kernel estimates in properties (G)(ii)--(iii) of
+\cite{IshigeKawakamiMichihisa2017} give, with constants depending on the
+chosen stable scale,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}
+ c(1+|y|)^{-\beta}\le p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)
+ \le C(1+|y|)^{-\beta},\qquad
+ |\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)|
+ \le C_\eta(1+|y|)^{-\beta-|\eta|}.
+\end{equation}
+In particular every quotient
+\(\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}/p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) is bounded.  The upper
+bound in \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} follows from
+\[
+ \begin{aligned}
+ \int p_1(y-z)^q p_1(y)^{1-q}\dd y
+ &\le C\int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta q}
+              (1+|y|)^{\beta(q-1)}\dd y\\
+ &\le C(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+       \int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta}\dd y,
+ \end{aligned}
+\]
+where \(p_1=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) and
+\(1+|y|\le(1+|z|)(1+|y-z|)\).  The final integral is finite because
+\(\beta>d\).  For the lower bound, integrate over \(|y-z|\le1\) and use
+\eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}; this gives the claimed power
+for \(|z|\ge2\).  Positivity and continuity on bounded \(z\)-sets complete
+the estimate.
+
+For \(|z|\le1\), \eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds} also gives
+\(p_1(y-\theta z)\le C p_1(y)\), uniformly in \(0\le\theta\le1\).
+Taylor's formula along the segment from \(y\) to \(y-z\), followed by the
+derivative bound in \eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}, therefore
+gives the pointwise bound
+\(|F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)|\le C|z|^{m+1}\), uniformly
+in \(y\).  For \(|z|>1\), \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} gives
+\(\|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_q\le C|z|^{\beta(1-1/q)}\).  The Taylor
+coefficients are bounded, so
+\(\|T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_q\le C|z|^m\).  Finally,
+\[
+ \beta(1-1/q)\le p,\qquad m\le p<m+1,
+\]
+with equality in the first relation when \(\beta>4\).  These observations
+prove \eqref{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}.
+\end{proof}

+
+## Stable-Kernel Critical-Moment Search
+
+Checked 2026-08-08 (Asia/Singapore).  The search target was the optimal
+absolute-moment hypothesis for the covariance-order relative-entropy
+asymptotic of a fixed law smoothed by an isotropic strictly alpha-stable
+kernel, with the stable kernel itself as the translated reference.
+
+The nearest paper was inspected in full:
+
+- K. Ishige, T. Kawakami, and H. Michihisa, *Asymptotic Expansions of
+  Solutions of Fractional Diffusion Equations*, SIAM J. Math. Anal. 49
+  (2017), 2167--2190, arXiv:1610.09789,
+  DOI 10.1137/16M1101428.
+- K. Ishige and T. Kawakami, *Refined Asymptotic Expansions of Solutions to
+  Fractional Diffusion Equations*, J. Dynam. Differential Equations 36
+  (2024), 2679--2702, arXiv:2109.14193,
+  DOI 10.1007/s10884-022-10224-4.
+
+Their theorems, bibliographies, and forward-citation records were checked,
+along with Crossref, Semantic Scholar, zbMATH, and targeted arXiv searches
+for combinations of stable/fractional heat kernels, translated density
+quotients, relative entropy, asymptotic expansions, and moment conditions.
+The arXiv API returned HTTP 429 during this audit, so arXiv abstract pages,
+HTML, and PDFs were used to inspect the relevant records.  Google Scholar
+was also queried but returned its unusual-traffic interstitial; no Scholar
+results are therefore represented as inspected.
+
+Ishige--Kawakami--Michihisa prove density-level fractional-heat expansions:
+moment-weighted kernel derivatives are subtracted and the remainder is
+controlled in scaled L^q and weighted L^1 norms.  The refined paper extends
+that framework to inhomogeneous and nonlinear equations.  Neither paper
+states the critical matched-quotient estimate
+
+\[
+\left\|\frac{p_1(\mathord\cdot-z)}{p_1}\right\|_{L^q(p_1)}^q
+\asymp (1+|z|)^{(d+\alpha)(q-1)},
+\]
+
+uses it to transfer a moment expansion through relative entropy, or gives
+the uniform sufficient exponent
+
+\[
+p_{\alpha,d}=\max\left\{2,
+\frac{4(d+\alpha)}{d+\alpha+4}\right\}.
+\]
+
+The stable-entropy papers of Bobkov--Chistyakov--Goetze, Johnson, and
+Toscani concern convergence of normalized convolution sequences or entropy
+relative to a fixed stable target.  They do not address this fixed-input,
+large-spatial-scale, moving matched-reference problem.  No indexed source
+located in the audit states the exponent or the matching uniform
+moment-class optimality result.  This remains a qualified negative search,
+not a proof of absence from every publication.

+For \(0<\alpha<2\), let \(p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) be the density of any
+centred isotropic strictly \(\alpha\)-stable law on \(\RR^d\), and use the
+spatial-scale normalization
+\[
+ p_s^{(\alpha,d)}(x)=s^{-d}p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(x/s),\qquad s>0.
+\]
+Changing the scale parameter in the characteristic exponent only changes
+the choice of \(p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\), so this notation covers every isotropic
+strictly stable kernel.  Put
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-critical-exponents}
+ \beta=d+\alpha,\qquad
+ q_{\alpha,d}:=\min\left\{2,1+\frac4\beta\right\},\qquad
+ p_{\alpha,d}:=\frac4{q_{\alpha,d}}
+ =\max\left\{2,\frac{4(d+\alpha)}{d+\alpha+4}\right\}.
+\end{equation}
+Write \(\Omega_{\alpha,d}(\dd y)=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)\dd y\) and
+\[
+ F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)
+ :=\frac{p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y-z)}{p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)}.

+\begin{lemma}[Stable critical translation remainder]
+\label{lem:stable-critical-translation-remainder}
+Let \(d\ge1\), \(0<\alpha<2\), \(p=p_{\alpha,d}\),
+\(q=q_{\alpha,d}\), and \(m=\lfloor p\rfloor\).  If
+\(T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)\) is the Taylor polynomial of
+\(F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\) at \(z=0\) through degree \(m\), then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth}
+ c_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+ \le \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}^q
+ \le C_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}.
+\end{equation}
+Moreover,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}
+ \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}
+ \begin{cases}
+  |z|^{m+1},&|z|\le1,\\
+  |z|^p,&|z|>1,
+ \end{cases}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}|z|^p.
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The standard stable-kernel estimates in properties (G)(ii)--(iii) of
+\cite{IshigeKawakamiMichihisa2017} give, with constants depending on the
+chosen stable scale,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}
+ c(1+|y|)^{-\beta}\le p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)
+ \le C(1+|y|)^{-\beta},\qquad
+ |\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)|
+ \le C_\eta(1+|y|)^{-\beta-|\eta|}.
+\end{equation}
+In particular every quotient
+\(\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}/p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) is bounded.  The upper
+bound in \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} follows from
+\[
+ \begin{aligned}
+ \int p_1(y-z)^q p_1(y)^{1-q}\dd y
+ &\le C\int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta q}
+              (1+|y|)^{\beta(q-1)}\dd y\\
+ &\le C(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+       \int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta}\dd y,
+ \end{aligned}
+\]
+where \(p_1=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) and
+\(1+|y|\le(1+|z|)(1+|y-z|)\).  The final integral is finite because
+\(\beta>d\).  For the lower bound, integrate over \(|y-z|\le1\) and use
+\eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}; this gives the claimed power
+for \(|z|\ge2\).  Positivity and continuity on bounded \(z\)-sets complete
+the estimate.
+
+For \(|z|\le1\), \eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds} also gives
+\(p_1(y-\theta z)\le C p_1(y)\), uniformly in \(0\le\theta\le1\).
+Taylor's formula along the segment from \(y\) to \(y-z\), followed by the
+derivative bound in \eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}, therefore
+gives the pointwise bound
+\(|F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)|\le C|z|^{m+1}\), uniformly
+in \(y\).  For \(|z|>1\), \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} gives
+\(\|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_q\le C|z|^{\beta(1-1/q)}\).  The Taylor
+coefficients are bounded, so
+\(\|T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_q\le C|z|^m\).  Finally,
+\[
+ \beta(1-1/q)\le p,\qquad m\le p<m+1,
+\]
+with equality in the first relation when \(\beta>4\).  These observations
+prove \eqref{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}.
+\end{proof}

+We first prove the obstruction below two moments.  If
+\(\limsup_{s\to\infty}s^4H_{\alpha,d}(s)<\infty\), Pinsker's inequality
+and scaling give, for every fixed \(\xi\in\RR^d\),
+\[
+ |\widehat p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(\xi)|
+ |\varphi_X(\xi/s)-1|
+ \le \|p_1^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu_s-p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\|_1
+ \le \sqrt{2H_{\alpha,d}(s)}=O(s^{-2}),
+\]
+where \(\nu_s\) is the law of \(X/s\).  Since the stable characteristic
+function never vanishes, take \(\xi=e\) for a unit vector \(e\), multiply
+the real part by \(s^2\), and use Fatou's lemma to obtain
+\[
+ \frac12\EE(e\cdot X)^2
+ \le \liminf_{s\to\infty}s^2
+       \EE[1-\cos((e\cdot X)/s)]<\infty.
+\]

+\(n^{-a-1}\) at \(\pm ne_1\), with the remaining mass at zero.  This law
+has mean zero and finite \(r\)th moment but infinite variance, so its scaled
+entropy has infinite limsup.

+Fix \(2\le r<p\), choose positive \(a_j\) with \(\sum_ja_j<\infty\), and
+put symmetric masses \(w_j/2\) at \(\pm R_je_1\), where
+\(w_j=a_jR_j^{-r}\).  Add a sufficiently small bounded symmetric spanning
+component.  The resulting law has positive-definite finite covariance and

+ A_j=B(R_je_1,s_j).
+\]
+The component at \(R_je_1\) gives
+\((p_{s_j}^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu)(A_j)\ge c_{\alpha,d}w_j\).  On the other hand,
+\eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds} and \(s_j/R_j\to0\) give
+\[
+ p_{s_j}^{(\alpha,d)}(A_j)
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}(s_j/R_j)^\beta
+ =C_{\alpha,d}\kappa^\beta w_j.
+\]
+Choose \(\kappa\) so that the second Bernoulli mass is a fixed small
+fraction of the first.  Data processing to
+\(\{A_j,A_j^c\}\) then yields \(H_{\alpha,d}(s_j)\ge c w_j\), and hence

 \]

 \end{proof}

 As above, this is a documented negative search rather than a logically
 exhaustive proof of absence from all literature.
+
+## Stable-Kernel Critical-Moment Search
+
+Checked 2026-08-08 (Asia/Singapore).  The search target was the optimal
+absolute-moment hypothesis for the covariance-order relative-entropy
+asymptotic of a fixed law smoothed by an isotropic strictly alpha-stable
+kernel, with the stable kernel itself as the translated reference.
+
+The nearest paper was inspected in full:
+
+- K. Ishige, T. Kawakami, and H. Michihisa, *Asymptotic Expansions of
+  Solutions of Fractional Diffusion Equations*, SIAM J. Math. Anal. 49
+  (2017), 2167--2190, arXiv:1610.09789,
+  DOI 10.1137/16M1101428.
+- K. Ishige and T. Kawakami, *Refined Asymptotic Expansions of Solutions to
+  Fractional Diffusion Equations*, J. Dynam. Differential Equations 36
+  (2024), 2679--2702, arXiv:2109.14193,
+  DOI 10.1007/s10884-022-10224-4.
+
+Their theorems, bibliographies, and forward-citation records were checked,
+along with Crossref, Semantic Scholar, zbMATH, and targeted arXiv searches
+for combinations of stable/fractional heat kernels, translated density
+quotients, relative entropy, asymptotic expansions, and moment conditions.
+The arXiv API returned HTTP 429 during this audit, so arXiv abstract pages,
+HTML, and PDFs were used to inspect the relevant records.  Google Scholar
+was also queried but returned its unusual-traffic interstitial; no Scholar
+results are therefore represented as inspected.
+
+Ishige--Kawakami--Michihisa prove density-level fractional-heat expansions:
+moment-weighted kernel derivatives are subtracted and the remainder is
+controlled in scaled L^q and weighted L^1 norms.  The refined paper extends
+that framework to inhomogeneous and nonlinear equations.  Neither paper
+states the critical matched-quotient estimate
+
+\[
+\left\|\frac{p_1(\mathord\cdot-z)}{p_1}\right\|_{L^q(p_1)}^q
+\asymp (1+|z|)^{(d+\alpha)(q-1)},
+\]
+
+uses it to transfer a moment expansion through relative entropy, or gives
+the uniform sufficient exponent
+
+\[
+p_{\alpha,d}=\max\left\{2,
+\frac{4(d+\alpha)}{d+\alpha+4}\right\}.
+\]
+
+The stable-entropy papers of Bobkov--Chistyakov--Goetze, Johnson, and
+Toscani concern convergence of normalized convolution sequences or entropy
+relative to a fixed stable target.  They do not address this fixed-input,
+large-spatial-scale, moving matched-reference problem.  No indexed source
+located in the audit states the exponent or the matching uniform
+moment-class optimality result.  This remains a qualified negative search,
+not a proof of absence from every publication.

+    stable_rows = []

+            p_value = sp.simplify(4 / q_value)

+            translation_growth = sp.simplify(beta * (1 - 1 / q_value))

+\begin{lemma}[Stable critical translation remainder]
+\label{lem:stable-critical-translation-remainder}
+Let \(d\ge1\), \(0<\alpha<2\), \(p=p_{\alpha,d}\),
+\(q=q_{\alpha,d}\), and \(m=\lfloor p\rfloor\).  If
+\(T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)\) is the Taylor polynomial of
+\(F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\) at \(z=0\) through degree \(m\), then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth}
+ c_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+ \le \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}^q
+ \le C_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}.
+\end{equation}
+Moreover,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}
+ \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}
+ \begin{cases}
+  |z|^{m+1},&|z|\le1,\\
+  |z|^p,&|z|>1,
+ \end{cases}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}|z|^p.
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The standard stable-kernel estimates in properties (G)(ii)--(iii) of
+\cite{IshigeKawakamiMichihisa2017} give, with constants depending on the
+chosen stable scale,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}
+ c(1+|y|)^{-\beta}\le p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)
+ \le C(1+|y|)^{-\beta},\qquad
+ |\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)|
+ \le C_\eta(1+|y|)^{-\beta-|\eta|}.
+\end{equation}
+In particular every quotient
+\(\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}/p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) is bounded.  The upper
+bound in \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} follows from
+\[
+ \begin{aligned}
+ \int p_1(y-z)^q p_1(y)^{1-q}\dd y
+ &\le C\int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta q}
+              (1+|y|)^{\beta(q-1)}\dd y\\
+ &\le C(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+       \int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta}\dd y,
+ \end{aligned}
+\]
+where \(p_1=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) and
+\(1+|y|\le(1+|z|)(1+|y-z|)\).  The final integral is finite because
+\(\beta>d\).  For the lower bound, integrate over \(|y-z|\le1\) and use
+\eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}; this gives the claimed power
+for \(|z|\ge2\).  Positivity and continuity on bounded \(z\)-sets complete
+the estimate.
+
+For \(|z|\le1\), \eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds} also gives
+\(p_1(y-\theta z)\le C p_1(y)\), uniformly in \(0\le\theta\le1\).
+Taylor's formula along the segment from \(y\) to \(y-z\), followed by the
+derivative bound in \eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}, therefore
+gives the pointwise bound
+\(|F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)|\le C|z|^{m+1}\), uniformly
+in \(y\).  For \(|z|>1\), \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} gives
+\(\|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_q\le C|z|^{\beta(1-1/q)}\).  The Taylor
+coefficients are bounded, so
+\(\|T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_q\le C|z|^m\).  Finally,
+\[
+ \beta(1-1/q)\le p,\qquad m\le p<m+1,
+\]
+with equality in the first relation when \(\beta>4\).  These observations
+prove \eqref{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}.
+\end{proof}

 As above, this is a documented negative search rather than a logically
 exhaustive proof of absence from all literature.
+
+## Stable-Kernel Critical-Moment Search
+
+Checked 2026-08-08 (Asia/Singapore).  The search target was the optimal
+absolute-moment hypothesis for the covariance-order relative-entropy
+asymptotic of a fixed law smoothed by an isotropic strictly alpha-stable
+kernel, with the stable kernel itself as the translated reference.
+
+The nearest paper was inspected in full:
+
+- K. Ishige, T. Kawakami, and H. Michihisa, *Asymptotic Expansions of
+  Solutions of Fractional Diffusion Equations*, SIAM J. Math. Anal. 49
+  (2017), 2167--2190, arXiv:1610.09789,
+  DOI 10.1137/16M1101428.
+- K. Ishige and T. Kawakami, *Refined Asymptotic Expansions of Solutions to
+  Fractional Diffusion Equations*, J. Dynam. Differential Equations 36
+  (2024), 2679--2702, arXiv:2109.14193,
+  DOI 10.1007/s10884-022-10224-4.
+
+Their theorems, bibliographies, and forward-citation records were checked,
+along with Crossref, Semantic Scholar, zbMATH, and targeted arXiv searches
+for combinations of stable/fractional heat kernels, translated density
+quotients, relative entropy, asymptotic expansions, and moment conditions.
+The arXiv API returned HTTP 429 during this audit, so arXiv abstract pages,
+HTML, and PDFs were used to inspect the relevant records.  Google Scholar
+was also queried but returned its unusual-traffic interstitial; no Scholar
+results are therefore represented as inspected.
+
+Ishige--Kawakami--Michihisa prove density-level fractional-heat expansions:
+moment-weighted kernel derivatives are subtracted and the remainder is
+controlled in scaled L^q and weighted L^1 norms.  The refined paper extends
+that framework to inhomogeneous and nonlinear equations.  Neither paper
+states the critical matched-quotient estimate
+
+\[
+\left\|\frac{p_1(\mathord\cdot-z)}{p_1}\right\|_{L^q(p_1)}^q
+\asymp (1+|z|)^{(d+\alpha)(q-1)},
+\]
+
+uses it to transfer a moment expansion through relative entropy, or gives
+the uniform sufficient exponent
+
+\[
+p_{\alpha,d}=\max\left\{2,
+\frac{4(d+\alpha)}{d+\alpha+4}\right\}.
+\]
+
+The stable-entropy papers of Bobkov--Chistyakov--Goetze, Johnson, and
+Toscani concern convergence of normalized convolution sequences or entropy
+relative to a fixed stable target.  They do not address this fixed-input,
+large-spatial-scale, moving matched-reference problem.  No indexed source
+located in the audit states the exponent or the matching uniform
+moment-class optimality result.  This remains a qualified negative search,
+not a proof of absence from every publication.

+\end{equation}
+Write \(\Omega_{\alpha,d}(\dd y)=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)\dd y\) and

+ F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)

+\begin{lemma}[Stable critical translation remainder]
+\label{lem:stable-critical-translation-remainder}
+Let \(d\ge1\), \(0<\alpha<2\), \(p=p_{\alpha,d}\),
+\(q=q_{\alpha,d}\), and \(m=\lfloor p\rfloor\).  If
+\(T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)\) is the Taylor polynomial of
+\(F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\) at \(z=0\) through degree \(m\), then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth}
+ c_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+ \le \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}^q
+ \le C_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}.
+\end{equation}
+Moreover,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}
+ \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}
+ \begin{cases}
+  |z|^{m+1},&|z|\le1,\\
+  |z|^p,&|z|>1,
+ \end{cases}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}|z|^p.
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The standard stable-kernel estimates in properties (G)(ii)--(iii) of
+\cite{IshigeKawakamiMichihisa2017} give, with constants depending on the
+chosen stable scale,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}
+ c(1+|y|)^{-\beta}\le p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)
+ \le C(1+|y|)^{-\beta},\qquad
+ |\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)|
+ \le C_\eta(1+|y|)^{-\beta-|\eta|}.
+\end{equation}
+In particular every quotient
+\(\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}/p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) is bounded.  The upper
+bound in \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} follows from
+\[
+ \begin{aligned}
+ \int p_1(y-z)^q p_1(y)^{1-q}\dd y
+ &\le C\int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta q}
+              (1+|y|)^{\beta(q-1)}\dd y\\
+ &\le C(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+       \int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta}\dd y,
+ \end{aligned}
+\]
+where \(p_1=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) and
+\(1+|y|\le(1+|z|)(1+|y-z|)\).  The final integral is finite because
+\(\beta>d\).  For the lower bound, integrate over \(|y-z|\le1\) and use
+\eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}; this gives the claimed power
+for \(|z|\ge2\).  Positivity and continuity on bounded \(z\)-sets complete
+the estimate.
+
+For \(|z|\le1\), \eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds} also gives
+\(p_1(y-\theta z)\le C p_1(y)\), uniformly in \(0\le\theta\le1\).
+Taylor's formula along the segment from \(y\) to \(y-z\), followed by the
+derivative bound in \eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}, therefore
+gives the pointwise bound
+\(|F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)|\le C|z|^{m+1}\), uniformly
+in \(y\).  For \(|z|>1\), \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} gives
+\(\|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_q\le C|z|^{\beta(1-1/q)}\).  The Taylor
+coefficients are bounded, so
+\(\|T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_q\le C|z|^m\).  Finally,
+\[
+ \beta(1-1/q)\le p,\qquad m\le p<m+1,
+\]
+with equality in the first relation when \(\beta>4\).  These observations
+prove \eqref{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}.
+\end{proof}

+\((p_{s_j}^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu)(A_j)\ge c_{\alpha,d}w_j\).  On the other hand,
+\eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds} and \(s_j/R_j\to0\) give
+\[
+ p_{s_j}^{(\alpha,d)}(A_j)
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}(s_j/R_j)^\beta
+ =C_{\alpha,d}\kappa^\beta w_j.
+\]
+Choose \(\kappa\) so that the second Bernoulli mass is a fixed small
+fraction of the first.  Data processing to
+\(\{A_j,A_j^c\}\) then yields \(H_{\alpha,d}(s_j)\ge c w_j\), and hence
 \[
- t_j^4H_d(t_j)\ge c_dR_j^4w_j^{1+4/(d+1)}
- =c_d\alpha_j^{q_d}R_j^{4-rq_d}.
+ s_j^4H_{\alpha,d}(s_j)
+ \ge cR_j^4w_j^{1+4/\beta}
+ =ca_j^{q_{\alpha,d}}R_j^{4-rq_{\alpha,d}}.
 \]
-Since \(r<p_d=4/q_d\), the exponent of \(R_j\) is positive.  Recursive
-choice of the radii makes this expression unbounded while preserving the
-finite \(r\)th moment and, after adding a bounded spanning component, a
-positive-definite covariance.
+Here \(q_{\alpha,d}=1+4/\beta\) and
+\(r<p=4/q_{\alpha,d}\), so the exponent of \(R_j\) is positive.
+Recursive choice of the radii makes \(s_j\to\infty\) and the last display
+unbounded while preserving all moment assertions.
 \end{proof}

 As above, this is a documented negative search rather than a logically
 exhaustive proof of absence from all literature.
+
+## Stable-Kernel Critical-Moment Search
+
+Checked 2026-08-08 (Asia/Singapore).  The search target was the optimal
+absolute-moment hypothesis for the covariance-order relative-entropy
+asymptotic of a fixed law smoothed by an isotropic strictly alpha-stable
+kernel, with the stable kernel itself as the translated reference.
+
+The nearest paper was inspected in full:
+
+- K. Ishige, T. Kawakami, and H. Michihisa, *Asymptotic Expansions of
+  Solutions of Fractional Diffusion Equations*, SIAM J. Math. Anal. 49
+  (2017), 2167--2190, arXiv:1610.09789,
+  DOI 10.1137/16M1101428.
+- K. Ishige and T. Kawakami, *Refined Asymptotic Expansions of Solutions to
+  Fractional Diffusion Equations*, J. Dynam. Differential Equations 36
+  (2024), 2679--2702, arXiv:2109.14193,
+  DOI 10.1007/s10884-022-10224-4.
+
+Their theorems, bibliographies, and forward-citation records were checked,
+along with Crossref, Semantic Scholar, zbMATH, and targeted arXiv searches
+for combinations of stable/fractional heat kernels, translated density
+quotients, relative entropy, asymptotic expansions, and moment conditions.
+The arXiv API returned HTTP 429 during this audit, so arXiv abstract pages,
+HTML, and PDFs were used to inspect the relevant records.  Google Scholar
+was also queried but returned its unusual-traffic interstitial; no Scholar
+results are therefore represented as inspected.
+
+Ishige--Kawakami--Michihisa prove density-level fractional-heat expansions:
+moment-weighted kernel derivatives are subtracted and the remainder is
+controlled in scaled L^q and weighted L^1 norms.  The refined paper extends
+that framework to inhomogeneous and nonlinear equations.  Neither paper
+states the critical matched-quotient estimate
+
+\[
+\left\|\frac{p_1(\mathord\cdot-z)}{p_1}\right\|_{L^q(p_1)}^q
+\asymp (1+|z|)^{(d+\alpha)(q-1)},
+\]
+
+uses it to transfer a moment expansion through relative entropy, or gives
+the uniform sufficient exponent
+
+\[
+p_{\alpha,d}=\max\left\{2,
+\frac{4(d+\alpha)}{d+\alpha+4}\right\}.
+\]
+
+The stable-entropy papers of Bobkov--Chistyakov--Goetze, Johnson, and
+Toscani concern convergence of normalized convolution sequences or entropy
+relative to a fixed stable target.  They do not address this fixed-input,
+large-spatial-scale, moving matched-reference problem.  No indexed source
+located in the audit states the exponent or the matching uniform
+moment-class optimality result.  This remains a qualified negative search,
+not a proof of absence from every publication.

+\begin{lemma}[Stable critical translation remainder]
+\label{lem:stable-critical-translation-remainder}
+Let \(d\ge1\), \(0<\alpha<2\), \(p=p_{\alpha,d}\),
+\(q=q_{\alpha,d}\), and \(m=\lfloor p\rfloor\).  If
+\(T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)\) is the Taylor polynomial of
+\(F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\) at \(z=0\) through degree \(m\), then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth}
+ c_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+ \le \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}^q
+ \le C_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}.
+\end{equation}
+Moreover,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}
+ \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}
+ \begin{cases}
+  |z|^{m+1},&|z|\le1,\\
+  |z|^p,&|z|>1,
+ \end{cases}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}|z|^p.
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The standard stable-kernel estimates in properties (G)(ii)--(iii) of
+\cite{IshigeKawakamiMichihisa2017} give, with constants depending on the
+chosen stable scale,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}
+ c(1+|y|)^{-\beta}\le p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)
+ \le C(1+|y|)^{-\beta},\qquad
+ |\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)|
+ \le C_\eta(1+|y|)^{-\beta-|\eta|}.
+\end{equation}
+In particular every quotient
+\(\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}/p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) is bounded.  The upper
+bound in \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} follows from
+\[
+ \begin{aligned}
+ \int p_1(y-z)^q p_1(y)^{1-q}\dd y
+ &\le C\int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta q}
+              (1+|y|)^{\beta(q-1)}\dd y\\
+ &\le C(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+       \int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta}\dd y,
+ \end{aligned}
+\]
+where \(p_1=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) and
+\(1+|y|\le(1+|z|)(1+|y-z|)\).  The final integral is finite because
+\(\beta>d\).  For the lower bound, integrate over \(|y-z|\le1\) and use
+\eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}; this gives the claimed power
+for \(|z|\ge2\).  Positivity and continuity on bounded \(z\)-sets complete
+the estimate.
+
+For \(|z|\le1\), \eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds} also gives
+\(p_1(y-\theta z)\le C p_1(y)\), uniformly in \(0\le\theta\le1\).
+Taylor's formula along the segment from \(y\) to \(y-z\), followed by the
+derivative bound in \eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}, therefore
+gives the pointwise bound
+\(|F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)|\le C|z|^{m+1}\), uniformly
+in \(y\).  For \(|z|>1\), \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} gives
+\(\|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_q\le C|z|^{\beta(1-1/q)}\).  The Taylor
+coefficients are bounded, so
+\(\|T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_q\le C|z|^m\).  Finally,
+\[
+ \beta(1-1/q)\le p,\qquad m\le p<m+1,
+\]
+with equality in the first relation when \(\beta>4\).  These observations
+prove \eqref{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}.
+\end{proof}

 As above, this is a documented negative search rather than a logically
 exhaustive proof of absence from all literature.
+
+## Stable-Kernel Critical-Moment Search
+
+Checked 2026-08-08 (Asia/Singapore).  The search target was the optimal
+absolute-moment hypothesis for the covariance-order relative-entropy
+asymptotic of a fixed law smoothed by an isotropic strictly alpha-stable
+kernel, with the stable kernel itself as the translated reference.
+
+The nearest paper was inspected in full:
+
+- K. Ishige, T. Kawakami, and H. Michihisa, *Asymptotic Expansions of
+  Solutions of Fractional Diffusion Equations*, SIAM J. Math. Anal. 49
+  (2017), 2167--2190, arXiv:1610.09789,
+  DOI 10.1137/16M1101428.
+- K. Ishige and T. Kawakami, *Refined Asymptotic Expansions of Solutions to
+  Fractional Diffusion Equations*, J. Dynam. Differential Equations 36
+  (2024), 2679--2702, arXiv:2109.14193,
+  DOI 10.1007/s10884-022-10224-4.
+
+Their theorems, bibliographies, and forward-citation records were checked,
+along with Crossref, Semantic Scholar, zbMATH, and targeted arXiv searches
+for combinations of stable/fractional heat kernels, translated density
+quotients, relative entropy, asymptotic expansions, and moment conditions.
+The arXiv API returned HTTP 429 during this audit, so arXiv abstract pages,
+HTML, and PDFs were used to inspect the relevant records.  Google Scholar
+was also queried but returned its unusual-traffic interstitial; no Scholar
+results are therefore represented as inspected.
+
+Ishige--Kawakami--Michihisa prove density-level fractional-heat expansions:
+moment-weighted kernel derivatives are subtracted and the remainder is
+controlled in scaled L^q and weighted L^1 norms.  The refined paper extends
+that framework to inhomogeneous and nonlinear equations.  Neither paper
+states the critical matched-quotient estimate
+
+\[
+\left\|\frac{p_1(\mathord\cdot-z)}{p_1}\right\|_{L^q(p_1)}^q
+\asymp (1+|z|)^{(d+\alpha)(q-1)},
+\]
+
+uses it to transfer a moment expansion through relative entropy, or gives
+the uniform sufficient exponent
+
+\[
+p_{\alpha,d}=\max\left\{2,
+\frac{4(d+\alpha)}{d+\alpha+4}\right\}.
+\]
+
+The stable-entropy papers of Bobkov--Chistyakov--Goetze, Johnson, and
+Toscani concern convergence of normalized convolution sequences or entropy
+relative to a fixed stable target.  They do not address this fixed-input,
+large-spatial-scale, moving matched-reference problem.  No indexed source
+located in the audit states the exponent or the matching uniform
+moment-class optimality result.  This remains a qualified negative search,
+not a proof of absence from every publication.

+\begin{lemma}[Stable critical translation remainder]
+\label{lem:stable-critical-translation-remainder}
+Let \(d\ge1\), \(0<\alpha<2\), \(p=p_{\alpha,d}\),
+\(q=q_{\alpha,d}\), and \(m=\lfloor p\rfloor\).  If
+\(T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)\) is the Taylor polynomial of
+\(F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\) at \(z=0\) through degree \(m\), then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth}
+ c_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+ \le \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}^q
+ \le C_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}.
+\end{equation}
+Moreover,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}
+ \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}
+ \begin{cases}
+  |z|^{m+1},&|z|\le1,\\
+  |z|^p,&|z|>1,
+ \end{cases}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}|z|^p.
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The standard stable-kernel estimates in properties (G)(ii)--(iii) of
+\cite{IshigeKawakamiMichihisa2017} give, with constants depending on the
+chosen stable scale,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}
+ c(1+|y|)^{-\beta}\le p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)
+ \le C(1+|y|)^{-\beta},\qquad
+ |\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)|
+ \le C_\eta(1+|y|)^{-\beta-|\eta|}.
+\end{equation}
+In particular every quotient
+\(\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}/p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) is bounded.  The upper
+bound in \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} follows from
+\[
+ \begin{aligned}
+ \int p_1(y-z)^q p_1(y)^{1-q}\dd y
+ &\le C\int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta q}
+              (1+|y|)^{\beta(q-1)}\dd y\\
+ &\le C(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+       \int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta}\dd y,
+ \end{aligned}
+\]
+where \(p_1=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) and
+\(1+|y|\le(1+|z|)(1+|y-z|)\).  The final integral is finite because
+\(\beta>d\).  For the lower bound, integrate over \(|y-z|\le1\) and use
+\eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}; this gives the claimed power
+for \(|z|\ge2\).  Positivity and continuity on bounded \(z\)-sets complete
+the estimate.
+
+For \(|z|\le1\), \eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds} also gives
+\(p_1(y-\theta z)\le C p_1(y)\), uniformly in \(0\le\theta\le1\).
+Taylor's formula along the segment from \(y\) to \(y-z\), followed by the
+derivative bound in \eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}, therefore
+gives the pointwise bound
+\(|F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)|\le C|z|^{m+1}\), uniformly
+in \(y\).  For \(|z|>1\), \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} gives
+\(\|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_q\le C|z|^{\beta(1-1/q)}\).  The Taylor
+coefficients are bounded, so
+\(\|T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_q\le C|z|^m\).  Finally,
+\[
+ \beta(1-1/q)\le p,\qquad m\le p<m+1,
+\]
+with equality in the first relation when \(\beta>4\).  These observations
+prove \eqref{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}.
+\end{proof}

 As above, this is a documented negative search rather than a logically
 exhaustive proof of absence from all literature.
+
+## Stable-Kernel Critical-Moment Search
+
+Checked 2026-08-08 (Asia/Singapore).  The search target was the optimal
+absolute-moment hypothesis for the covariance-order relative-entropy
+asymptotic of a fixed law smoothed by an isotropic strictly alpha-stable
+kernel, with the stable kernel itself as the translated reference.
+
+The nearest paper was inspected in full:
+
+- K. Ishige, T. Kawakami, and H. Michihisa, *Asymptotic Expansions of
+  Solutions of Fractional Diffusion Equations*, SIAM J. Math. Anal. 49
+  (2017), 2167--2190, arXiv:1610.09789,
+  DOI 10.1137/16M1101428.
+- K. Ishige and T. Kawakami, *Refined Asymptotic Expansions of Solutions to
+  Fractional Diffusion Equations*, J. Dynam. Differential Equations 36
+  (2024), 2679--2702, arXiv:2109.14193,
+  DOI 10.1007/s10884-022-10224-4.
+
+Their theorems, bibliographies, and forward-citation records were checked,
+along with Crossref, Semantic Scholar, zbMATH, and targeted arXiv searches
+for combinations of stable/fractional heat kernels, translated density
+quotients, relative entropy, asymptotic expansions, and moment conditions.
+The arXiv API returned HTTP 429 during this audit, so arXiv abstract pages,
+HTML, and PDFs were used to inspect the relevant records.  Google Scholar
+was also queried but returned its unusual-traffic interstitial; no Scholar
+results are therefore represented as inspected.
+
+Ishige--Kawakami--Michihisa prove density-level fractional-heat expansions:
+moment-weighted kernel derivatives are subtracted and the remainder is
+controlled in scaled L^q and weighted L^1 norms.  The refined paper extends
+that framework to inhomogeneous and nonlinear equations.  Neither paper
+states the critical matched-quotient estimate
+
+\[
+\left\|\frac{p_1(\mathord\cdot-z)}{p_1}\right\|_{L^q(p_1)}^q
+\asymp (1+|z|)^{(d+\alpha)(q-1)},
+\]
+
+uses it to transfer a moment expansion through relative entropy, or gives
+the uniform sufficient exponent
+
+\[
+p_{\alpha,d}=\max\left\{2,
+\frac{4(d+\alpha)}{d+\alpha+4}\right\}.
+\]
+
+The stable-entropy papers of Bobkov--Chistyakov--Goetze, Johnson, and
+Toscani concern convergence of normalized convolution sequences or entropy
+relative to a fixed stable target.  They do not address this fixed-input,
+large-spatial-scale, moving matched-reference problem.  No indexed source
+located in the audit states the exponent or the matching uniform
+moment-class optimality result.  This remains a qualified negative search,
+not a proof of absence from every publication.
