+\begin{lemma}[Stable critical translation remainder]
+\label{lem:stable-critical-translation-remainder}
+Let \(d\ge1\), \(0<\alpha<2\), \(p=p_{\alpha,d}\),
+\(q=q_{\alpha,d}\), and \(m=\lfloor p\rfloor\).  If
+\(T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)\) is the Taylor polynomial of
+\(F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\) at \(z=0\) through degree \(m\), then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth}
+ c_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+ \le \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}^q
+ \le C_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}.
+\end{equation}
+Moreover,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}
+ \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}
+ \begin{cases}
+  |z|^{m+1},&|z|\le1,\\
+  |z|^p,&|z|>1,
+ \end{cases}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}|z|^p.
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The standard stable-kernel estimates in properties (G)(ii)--(iii) of
+\cite{IshigeKawakamiMichihisa2017} give, with constants depending on the
+chosen stable scale,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}
+ c(1+|y|)^{-\beta}\le p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)
+ \le C(1+|y|)^{-\beta},\qquad
+ |\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)|
+ \le C_\eta(1+|y|)^{-\beta-|\eta|}.
+\end{equation}
+In particular every quotient
+\(\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}/p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) is bounded.  The upper
+bound in \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} follows from
+\[
+ \begin{aligned}
+ \int p_1(y-z)^q p_1(y)^{1-q}\dd y
+ &\le C\int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta q}
+              (1+|y|)^{\beta(q-1)}\dd y\\
+ &\le C(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+       \int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta}\dd y,
+ \end{aligned}
+\]
+where \(p_1=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) and
+\(1+|y|\le(1+|z|)(1+|y-z|)\).  The final integral is finite because
+\(\beta>d\).  For the lower bound, integrate over \(|y-z|\le1\) and use
+\eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}; this gives the claimed power
+for \(|z|\ge2\).  Positivity and continuity on bounded \(z\)-sets complete
+the estimate.
+
+For \(|z|\le1\), \eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds} also gives
+\(p_1(y-\theta z)\le C p_1(y)\), uniformly in \(0\le\theta\le1\).
+Taylor's formula along the segment from \(y\) to \(y-z\), followed by the
+derivative bound in \eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}, therefore
+gives the pointwise bound
+\(|F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)|\le C|z|^{m+1}\), uniformly
+in \(y\).  For \(|z|>1\), \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} gives
+\(\|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_q\le C|z|^{\beta(1-1/q)}\).  The Taylor
+coefficients are bounded, so
+\(\|T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_q\le C|z|^m\).  Finally,
+\[
+ \beta(1-1/q)\le p,\qquad m\le p<m+1,
+\]
+with equality in the first relation when \(\beta>4\).  These observations
+prove \eqref{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}.
+\end{proof}

+
+## Stable-Kernel Critical-Moment Search
+
+Checked 2026-08-08 (Asia/Singapore).  The search target was the optimal
+absolute-moment hypothesis for the covariance-order relative-entropy
+asymptotic of a fixed law smoothed by an isotropic strictly alpha-stable
+kernel, with the stable kernel itself as the translated reference.
+
+The nearest paper was inspected in full:
+
+- K. Ishige, T. Kawakami, and H. Michihisa, *Asymptotic Expansions of
+  Solutions of Fractional Diffusion Equations*, SIAM J. Math. Anal. 49
+  (2017), 2167--2190, arXiv:1610.09789,
+  DOI 10.1137/16M1101428.
+- K. Ishige and T. Kawakami, *Refined Asymptotic Expansions of Solutions to
+  Fractional Diffusion Equations*, J. Dynam. Differential Equations 36
+  (2024), 2679--2702, arXiv:2109.14193,
+  DOI 10.1007/s10884-022-10224-4.
+
+Their theorems, bibliographies, and forward-citation records were checked,
+along with Crossref, Semantic Scholar, zbMATH, and targeted arXiv searches
+for combinations of stable/fractional heat kernels, translated density
+quotients, relative entropy, asymptotic expansions, and moment conditions.
+The arXiv API returned HTTP 429 during this audit, so arXiv abstract pages,
+HTML, and PDFs were used to inspect the relevant records.  Google Scholar
+was also queried but returned its unusual-traffic interstitial; no Scholar
+results are therefore represented as inspected.
+
+Ishige--Kawakami--Michihisa prove density-level fractional-heat expansions:
+moment-weighted kernel derivatives are subtracted and the remainder is
+controlled in scaled L^q and weighted L^1 norms.  The refined paper extends
+that framework to inhomogeneous and nonlinear equations.  Neither paper
+states the critical matched-quotient estimate
+
+\[
+\left\|\frac{p_1(\mathord\cdot-z)}{p_1}\right\|_{L^q(p_1)}^q
+\asymp (1+|z|)^{(d+\alpha)(q-1)},
+\]
+
+uses it to transfer a moment expansion through relative entropy, or gives
+the uniform sufficient exponent
+
+\[
+p_{\alpha,d}=\max\left\{2,
+\frac{4(d+\alpha)}{d+\alpha+4}\right\}.
+\]
+
+The stable-entropy papers of Bobkov--Chistyakov--Goetze, Johnson, and
+Toscani concern convergence of normalized convolution sequences or entropy
+relative to a fixed stable target.  They do not address this fixed-input,
+large-spatial-scale, moving matched-reference problem.  No indexed source
+located in the audit states the exponent or the matching uniform
+moment-class optimality result.  This remains a qualified negative search,
+not a proof of absence from every publication.

+Write \(\Omega_{\alpha,d}(\dd y)=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)\dd y\) and

+ F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)

+\begin{lemma}[Stable critical translation remainder]
+\label{lem:stable-critical-translation-remainder}
+Let \(d\ge1\), \(0<\alpha<2\), \(p=p_{\alpha,d}\),
+\(q=q_{\alpha,d}\), and \(m=\lfloor p\rfloor\).  If
+\(T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)\) is the Taylor polynomial of
+\(F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\) at \(z=0\) through degree \(m\), then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth}
+ c_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+ \le \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}^q
+ \le C_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}.
+\end{equation}
+Moreover,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}
+ \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}
+ \begin{cases}
+  |z|^{m+1},&|z|\le1,\\
+  |z|^p,&|z|>1,
+ \end{cases}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}|z|^p.
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The standard stable-kernel estimates in properties (G)(ii)--(iii) of
+\cite{IshigeKawakamiMichihisa2017} give, with constants depending on the
+chosen stable scale,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}
+ c(1+|y|)^{-\beta}\le p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)
+ \le C(1+|y|)^{-\beta},\qquad
+ |\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)|
+ \le C_\eta(1+|y|)^{-\beta-|\eta|}.
+\end{equation}
+In particular every quotient
+\(\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}/p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) is bounded.  The upper
+bound in \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} follows from
+\[
+ \begin{aligned}
+ \int p_1(y-z)^q p_1(y)^{1-q}\dd y
+ &\le C\int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta q}
+              (1+|y|)^{\beta(q-1)}\dd y\\
+ &\le C(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+       \int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta}\dd y,
+ \end{aligned}
+\]
+where \(p_1=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) and
+\(1+|y|\le(1+|z|)(1+|y-z|)\).  The final integral is finite because
+\(\beta>d\).  For the lower bound, integrate over \(|y-z|\le1\) and use
+\eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}; this gives the claimed power
+for \(|z|\ge2\).  Positivity and continuity on bounded \(z\)-sets complete
+the estimate.
+
+For \(|z|\le1\), \eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds} also gives
+\(p_1(y-\theta z)\le C p_1(y)\), uniformly in \(0\le\theta\le1\).
+Taylor's formula along the segment from \(y\) to \(y-z\), followed by the
+derivative bound in \eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}, therefore
+gives the pointwise bound
+\(|F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)|\le C|z|^{m+1}\), uniformly
+in \(y\).  For \(|z|>1\), \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} gives
+\(\|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_q\le C|z|^{\beta(1-1/q)}\).  The Taylor
+coefficients are bounded, so
+\(\|T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_q\le C|z|^m\).  Finally,
+\[
+ \beta(1-1/q)\le p,\qquad m\le p<m+1,
+\]
+with equality in the first relation when \(\beta>4\).  These observations
+prove \eqref{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}.
+\end{proof}
+

**(a) Prior Art**

The audit covered Crossref, targeted arXiv searches and full-text records, Semantic Scholar, zbMATH, and the references and forward citations of the nearest papers. Google Scholar was queried but blocked by its unusual-traffic interstitial; the arXiv API returned HTTP 429, so the relevant arXiv HTML, abstract pages, and PDFs were inspected directly. The qualified audit is recorded in [literature_check.md](D:/omega/automath/papers/publication/2026_cayley_chebyshev_poisson_entropy_strip_rkhs_jfa/artifacts/literature_check.md:154).

The manuscript already cited Ishige–Kawakami–Michihisa, *Asymptotic Expansions of Solutions of Fractional Diffusion Equations*, and the Ishige–Kawakami refined follow-up. I strengthened the comparison in [sec_introduction.tex](D:/omega/automath/papers/publication/2026_cayley_chebyshev_poisson_entropy_strip_rkhs_jfa/sec_introduction.tex:142): those works prove fractional-heat density expansions in scaled \(L^q\) and weighted \(L^1\) norms, but do not prove the critical matched-quotient estimate or transfer it through KL entropy.

The stable-entropy literature located, including Bobkov–Chistyakov–Götze, Johnson, and Toscani, treats normalized convolution sequences or fixed stable targets. No inspected source states this moving matched-reference exponent or its uniform moment-class optimality. This is a documented negative search, not a claim of exhaustive absence.

**(b) Weakest Link**

The former “Sharp high-dimensional KL moment threshold” theorem is now titled “Optimal uniform sufficient moment exponent for stable KL asymptotics” in [sec_verified_A2_results.tex](D:/omega/automath/papers/publication/2026_cayley_chebyshev_poisson_entropy_strip_rkhs_jfa/sec_verified_A2_results.tex:974).

The theorem and all principal summaries now state exactly what is established: endpoint sufficiency plus counterexamples for every smaller moment class. They explicitly disclaim a law-by-law necessity criterion when \(d+\alpha>4\), and record the exact tail/nonlinear-defect characterization beyond the critical finite-moment class as open.

**(c) Upgrade Target**

Judgment: **attempted and proved**. The search did not reveal it as a known theorem or routine corollary, and the stable-density tail and derivative bounds supplied the missing analytic input.

**(d) Integrated Result**

For every \(d\ge1\), \(0<\alpha<2\), and isotropic strictly \(\alpha\)-stable spatial-scale kernel, the manuscript now proves that the optimal uniform sufficient absolute-moment exponent is
\[
p_{\alpha,d}=\max\!\left\{2,\frac{4(d+\alpha)}{d+\alpha+4}\right\}.
\]
The proof establishes the sharp translated-quotient growth, critical Taylor remainder, KL/Bregman transfer including the \(q=2\) endpoint, the covariance coefficient \(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d}(\Sigma)\), and uniform lower obstructions below the stated exponent. The abstract, Main Theorem B, introduction, hypothesis ledger, and prior-art appendix were updated consistently.

+Ishige--Kawakami--Michihisa prove density-level fractional-heat expansions:

+\]
+

+the uniform sufficient exponent
+
+\[
+p_{\alpha,d}=\max\left\{2,
+\frac{4(d+\alpha)}{d+\alpha+4}\right\}.
+\]
+
+The stable-entropy papers of Bobkov--Chistyakov--Goetze, Johnson, and
+Toscani concern convergence of normalized convolution sequences or entropy
+relative to a fixed stable target.  They do not address this fixed-input,
+large-spatial-scale, moving matched-reference problem.  No indexed source

+moment-class optimality result.  This remains a qualified negative search,
+not a proof of absence from every publication.

+\end{equation}
+Write \(\Omega_{\alpha,d}(\dd y)=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)\dd y\) and

+ F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)

+\begin{lemma}[Stable critical translation remainder]
+\label{lem:stable-critical-translation-remainder}
+Let \(d\ge1\), \(0<\alpha<2\), \(p=p_{\alpha,d}\),
+\(q=q_{\alpha,d}\), and \(m=\lfloor p\rfloor\).  If
+\(T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)\) is the Taylor polynomial of
+\(F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\) at \(z=0\) through degree \(m\), then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth}
+ c_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+ \le \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}^q
+ \le C_{\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}.
+\end{equation}
+Moreover,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}
+ \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}
+ \begin{cases}
+  |z|^{m+1},&|z|\le1,\\
+  |z|^p,&|z|>1,
+ \end{cases}
+ \le C_{\alpha,d}|z|^p.
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The standard stable-kernel estimates in properties (G)(ii)--(iii) of
+\cite{IshigeKawakamiMichihisa2017} give, with constants depending on the
+chosen stable scale,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}
+ c(1+|y|)^{-\beta}\le p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)
+ \le C(1+|y|)^{-\beta},\qquad
+ |\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)|
+ \le C_\eta(1+|y|)^{-\beta-|\eta|}.
+\end{equation}
+In particular every quotient
+\(\partial^\eta p_1^{(\alpha,d)}/p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) is bounded.  The upper
+bound in \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} follows from
+\[
+ \begin{aligned}
+ \int p_1(y-z)^q p_1(y)^{1-q}\dd y
+ &\le C\int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta q}
+              (1+|y|)^{\beta(q-1)}\dd y\\
+ &\le C(1+|z|)^{\beta(q-1)}
+       \int(1+|y-z|)^{-\beta}\dd y,
+ \end{aligned}
+\]
+where \(p_1=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) and
+\(1+|y|\le(1+|z|)(1+|y-z|)\).  The final integral is finite because
+\(\beta>d\).  For the lower bound, integrate over \(|y-z|\le1\) and use
+\eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}; this gives the claimed power
+for \(|z|\ge2\).  Positivity and continuity on bounded \(z\)-sets complete
+the estimate.
+
+For \(|z|\le1\), \eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds} also gives
+\(p_1(y-\theta z)\le C p_1(y)\), uniformly in \(0\le\theta\le1\).
+Taylor's formula along the segment from \(y\) to \(y-z\), followed by the
+derivative bound in \eqref{eq:stable-density-derivative-bounds}, therefore
+gives the pointwise bound
+\(|F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)|\le C|z|^{m+1}\), uniformly
+in \(y\).  For \(|z|>1\), \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} gives
+\(\|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_q\le C|z|^{\beta(1-1/q)}\).  The Taylor
+coefficients are bounded, so
+\(\|T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_q\le C|z|^m\).  Finally,
+\[
+ \beta(1-1/q)\le p,\qquad m\le p<m+1,
+\]
+with equality in the first relation when \(\beta>4\).  These observations
+prove \eqref{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}.
+\end{proof}

The manuscript already cited Ishige–Kawakami–Michihisa, *Asymptotic Expansions of Solutions of Fractional Diffusion Equations*, and the Ishige–Kawakami refined follow-up. I strengthened the comparison in [sec_introduction.tex](D:/omega/automath/papers/publication/2026_cayley_chebyshev_poisson_entropy_strip_rkhs_jfa/sec_introduction.tex:142): those works prove fractional-heat density expansions in scaled \(L^q\) and weighted \(L^1\) norms, but do not prove the critical matched-quotient estimate or transfer it through KL entropy.

The stable-entropy literature located, including Bobkov–Chistyakov–Götze, Johnson, and Toscani, treats normalized convolution sequences or fixed stable targets. No inspected source states this moving matched-reference exponent or its uniform moment-class optimality. This is a documented negative search, not a claim of exhaustive absence.

**(b) Weakest Link**

They explicitly disclaim a law-by-law necessity criterion when \(d+\alpha>4\), and record the exact tail/nonlinear-defect characterization beyond the critical finite-moment class as open.

**(c) Upgrade Target**

Judgment: **attempted and proved**. The search did not reveal it as a known theorem or routine corollary, and the stable-density tail and derivative bounds supplied the missing analytic input.

**(d) Integrated Result**

For every \(d\ge1\), \(0<\alpha<2\), and isotropic strictly \(\alpha\)-stable spatial-scale kernel, the manuscript now proves that the optimal uniform sufficient absolute-moment exponent is
\[
p_{\alpha,d}=\max\!\left\{2,\frac{4(d+\alpha)}{d+\alpha+4}\right\}.
\]
The proof establishes the sharp translated-quotient growth, critical Taylor remainder, KL/Bregman transfer including the \(q=2\) endpoint, the covariance coefficient \(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d}(\Sigma)\), and uniform lower obstructions below the stated exponent. The abstract, Main Theorem B, introduction, hypothesis ledger, and prior-art appendix were updated consistently.
